Interior of the stone chamber |alternate_name=Maruzuka Kofun / Miyajidake Ōtsuka | part_of={{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft}} |location=[[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Fukutsu City]], Miyajimoto-cho 1241 (Ōtsuka) (within the grounds of {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft}}) | coordinates = 33 | coordinates = 46 | coordinates = 51.10 | coordinates = 130 | coordinates = 29 | coordinates = 19.15 | omitted = JP-40 | type={{ill|Round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} | area=Diameter: 35 meters | burial={{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}}-type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | burial goods=Gilded bronze-headed tachi swords, gilded bronze horse gear, gilded bronze crown, glass plates, bronze ware, and numerous burial items | Satellite Tombs= | built=Mid-7th century | Interred_individual=Possibly {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善|12=draft}} | Tomb Classification= | Historic Site=Part of the National Historic site "{{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft}}" | Historic Site=Burial items (National Treasure) | notes=Second-largest stone chamber in Japan | map=Japan Fukuoka | type=Round mound | map_dot_label=Miyajidake Kofun | map_dot_label=right }} '''Miyajidake Kofun''' (宮地嶽古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fukutsu City|ja|福津市|12=draft}}, [[Fukuoka Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the Kofuns comprising the {{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft}}, designation1 as a National Historic site. The burial items excavated from the mound are classified as a National Treasure. This kofun is known for having the second-largest stone chamber in Japan and for the discovery of numerous luxurious burial items. This article also includes information on the [[Miyajidake Kofun#Miyajidake Cremation Tomb|Miyajidake Cremation Tomb]], whose burial items are also designation1 as National Treasures. == Overview == [[File:Fudo Shrine (No.3 of Okunomiya 8 Shrines) in Miyajidake Shrine.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fudō Shrine (Okunomiya of Miyajidake Shrine)}}{{small|The hall of worship is built in front of the stone chamber opening.}}]] Miyajidake Kofun is a large circular Kofun constructed on the southern slope (approximately 55 meters above sea level) of Mount Miyajidake (elevation 180.7 meters) in northern Fukuoka Prefecture{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Nearby, ancient cremation graves associated with Miyajidake are believed to exist, and the surrounding area once featured small Kofuns. On a hill across the Misogi Pond, the {{ill|Miyaji Idenoue Kofun|ja|宮司井手ノ上古墳|12=draft}} is located{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Currently, the site is worshipped as Fudō Shrine, an Okunomiya (inner shrine) of Miyajidake Shrine. The stone chamber was opened in the mid-Edo period, and burial items were excavated multiple times during the Shōwa era. Measured surveys of the chamber were conducted in 1937 and 1996 (Shōwa 12 and Heisei 8), but no full excavation has been carried out. While the Kofun has been modified over time, it is estimated to have originally been a circular mound approximately 35 meters in diameter{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}}-type horizontal stone chamber, which opens to the east. The chamber, with a total length of 23 meters, is the second-largest of its kind in Japan. Though no excavations have been conducted inside the chamber, burial items believed to have originally been stored there have been discovered nearby, including a gilded bronze-headed tachi sword nearly 3 meters long, a gilded bronze crown, gilded bronze horse gear, glass plates, bronze ware, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}}. These burial goods are notable for their exceptional quality and quantity, and the horse gear and crown, adorned with arabesque patterns, reflect rich international influences. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the mid-7th century, during the {{ill|final stage of the Kofun period|ja|古墳時代終末期|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}} (or in the early to mid-7th century"Evaluation of the Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster > Miyajidake Kofun," *Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster III*, Fukutsu City Board of Education, 2013. / early 7th century{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, TK217-style period). It is widely regarded as the tomb of a leader from the Munakata clan, an ancient clan in the Munakata region. The specific interred individual is often identified as {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善|12=draft}}. The combination of the massive stone chamber and the luxurious burial items makes Miyajidake Kofun one of Japan's representative Kofuns. The burial site was designation1 a National Historic site in 2005 (Heisei 17), and its burial items were designation1 a National Treasure in 1952 (Shōwa 27). Access to the interior of the stone chamber is currently restricted except during the three annual grand festivals. == Archaeological History == * In the first year of the [[Kanpō]] era ([[1741]]), the stone chamber was exposed due to a landslide during heavy rain (as documented in the {{ill|Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel|ja|筑前国続風土記拾遺|12=draft}} compiled during the [[Tenpō]] era ([[1830]]–[[1844]])){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In the 4th year of the [[Enkyō]] era ([[1747]]), the deity Fudō Myōō was enshrined at the back of the stone chamber (as documented in the 'Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel'){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In [[1930]] (the 5th year of the [[Shōwa]] era), ancillary facilities were constructed around the tumulus in conjunction with the shrine's relocation{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1934]] (Shōwa 9), equestrian gear and swords were excavated during the construction of the shrine office{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On September 18, [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), the equestrian gear was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), an accurate survey of the stone chamber was conducted (by Kagayama Takeshi){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a glass ossuary was excavated during afforestation work on the eastern side of the tumulus{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On October 25, [[1939]] (Shōwa 14), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1951]] (Shōwa 26), fragments of a crown were excavated in front of the dromos{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. ** On March 29, [[1952]] (Shōwa 27), the excavated burial goods were designation1 as National Treasures (new Category). ** On April 27, [[1961]] (Shōwa 36), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (new Category). * In [[1996]] (Heisei 8), the stone chamber was resurveyed (by Ikenoue Hiroshi and others, reported in [[1999]]){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On March 2, [[2005]] (Heisei 17), it was designation1 as a [[Historic site]] of Japan as part of the "[[Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster]]"{{National Heritage Database|401|3422|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster}}. == Mound == [[File:Miyajidake-Kofun 20161014.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}{{small|Today, stone rows encircle the mound.}}]] The mound was built by cutting through the gentle slope of a ridge and reshaping the natural terrain{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The current mound has an elliptical type, measuring 27 meters north-south and 34 meters east-west, but it is estimated to have originally been a circular type with a diameter of about 35 meters{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A secondary layer of earth, approximately 2 meters thick, is observed on the mound, which is believed to be the soil excavated during the 1934 digging of the stone chamber{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Around the mound, rows of stones about 1 meter wide and 1.4 meters high encircle the structure, with three-tiered stacking near the dromos{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. These stone rows were installed before 1934 and are believed to have reduced the original size of the mound{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == burial == [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-1.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Bird's-eye view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Expanded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility is a {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber with a side entrance|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}} type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening towards the east. Among the passageway and main chamber, the rear section of the main chamber is slightly narrower, divided into a rear chamber and a front chamber, showcasing a multi-chamber structure similar to horizontal stone chambers in the Kinai region. The area of the stone chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}: * Total length of the stone chamber: Approx. 23.1 meters (current measurement: 23.5–24 meters) * Stone sarcophagus (rear chamber): Length 3.5 meters, width approx. 1.75 meters * Main chamber (front chamber): Length 11.7 meters, width 2.5–2.8 meters, height 2.2–3.1 meters ** Left niche (south niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.5 meters ** Right niche (north niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.3 meters The stone material for the chamber is said to be conglomerate rock from the Koi no Ura coast{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Large stones were used, suggesting significant labor was required to transport them from the coast to the mid-slope area{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. The stone chamber is the second largest nationwide after the {{ill|Maruyama Kofun (Kashihara)|ja|丸山古墳 (橿原市)|12=draft}} (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture), with a total length of 28.4 meters. In the stone sarcophagus (first stone from the rear), three approximately 3-meter monolithic stones are assembled. The main chamber (second to fourth stones from the rear) features monolithic stones, 3.1–4.5 meters in height, standing side by side on both sidewalls{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Particularly on the second stone from the rear, niches have been carved into both sides of the stone, which is the largest stone in the chamber, measuring more than 1.7 meters in thickness{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Historical records from the Edo period indicate that these niches existed from the beginning{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The passageway (fifth to seventh stones from the rear) is constructed with two to three layers of stacked stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Near the entrance, stones 0.3–0.4 meters in size are irregularly piled, considered to be secondary stonework{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The floor, currently covered with concrete, was likely originally paved with pebbles and arranged with floor stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The ceiling stones measure 0.5 meters thick in the sarcophagus area, 1 meter above the second stone (niche area), and 1.65 meters above the fourth stone{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A similar stone chamber structure to the Miyajidake Kofun is known from the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳|12=draft}} in Fukutsu City. Previously, the Miyajidake Kofun was thought to precede the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, but based on investigations from 2010–2011 (Heisei 22–23), it is now hypothesized that the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun predates the Miyajidake Kofun{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Reference: Bird's-eye view of the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳|12=draft}} stone chamber Miyajidake Kofun, sekkaku.jpg|Stone sarcophagus and main chamber (towards the rear wall)
{{small|The rear sarcophagus stone is the first stone. Niches are formed on the sidewalls of the second stone in the main chamber.}} Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-1.jpg|Main chamber (towards the rear wall) Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-2.jpg|Main chamber (towards the entrance) Miyajidake Kofun, entrance.jpg|Entrance area (towards the rear wall) == burial goods == [[File:HARNESS MIYAJIDAKE.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Gilt Bronze Stirrup (National Treasure)}}]] The grave goods excavated near the tumulus during the Shōwa period are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Items owned by Miyajidake Shrine (formerly stored in the Tokyo National Museum, later deposited in the Kyushu National Museum, and designation1 as National Treasures) are marked with an "M." * Swords ** Large gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 2.4–2.8 meters. Parts including the pommel, guard, sheath fittings, and blade remain. ** Gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 0.90 meters. Parts including the pommel, habaki fitting, sheath tip fitting, and blade remain. * Horse gear ** Gilt bronze saddle fittings (M) - Front and rear bridges are mostly intact, but most other fittings are missing. ** Gilt bronze stirrups (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze bridles with decorative plates (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze pendants (pair) (M) ** Saddle with arabesque fittings (M) ** Iron fittings (M) ** Various other fittings (7 items, gilt bronze saddle fittings included) (M) * Glass plates ** Three intact plates (M) - Possibly raw materials for glass beads. ** 27 fragments (M19, others: 8+) * Whetstone (M) * Openwork gilt bronze crown (M) * Glass beads (large, medium) - Total: 265 (M256, others: 6). Made of lead glass, semi-transparent green. * Gold rings - Total: 3 (M1, others: 2) * Copper bells - Total: 3 (M2, others: 1) * Copper nails - Total: 4 (M) * Decorative metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Other metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Copper chain - 1 unit (18 links) (M) * Copper vessels - Total: 2 (M). Includes one copper bowl with a lid and one tray. * Copper utility knife with sheath fittings (M) * [[Sue pottery]] - Total: 17 (M4, others: 13). Includes six bowls, five lids, two tall stemmed vessels, and one flat bottle. Older Sue pottery types (before the Oda IVA period, TK209 type) are excluded{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. * [[Haji pottery]] - Total: 3 (M). Includes one bowl and two jars. == Burial Individual ==
'''Genealogical chart based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}''' {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||01| 01={{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi|12=draft}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||!|}} {{familytree|border=0|01|~|y|~|02| 01=Ōama no Ōji
({{Supra|40}} {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft}})|02={{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘|12=draft}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||!}} {{familytree|border=0||||01| 01={{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子|12=draft}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The individual buried in the Miyajidake Kofun is unknown, but they are presumed to be a chief of the ancient Munakata clan (宗形氏/宗像氏) from the Munakata region. Specifically, one theory identifies the buried individual as '''{{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi|12=draft}}''' (むなかたのきみとくぜん). Munakata Tokuyoshi is believed to have been the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子|12=draft}} (654?–696). According to the genealogical records in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, in the second year of Emperor Tenmu (673), Prince Ōama (later {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft}}) married Amako no Iratsume, the daughter of Munakata Tokuyoshi, producing Prince Takechi. While details are sparse due to limited mentions in other texts, Prince Takechi played a central role as the commander-in-chief of Emperor Ōama's forces during the Jinshin War and was later appointed {{ill|Daijō-daijin|ja|太政大臣|12=draft}} in 690 under Empress Jitō. Munakata Tokuyoshi is therefore thought to have been instrumental in advancing the Munakata clan's influence within the central government「Munakata Tokuyoshi」『Dictionary of Ancient Japanese Clans, Popular Edition』, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2010.. Prince Takechi died in 696, with records in the {{ill|Kuge Bunin|ja|Kugyō補任|12=draft}} stating he was 42 or 43 years old, while the {{ill|Fusō Ryakki|ja|扶桑略記|12=draft}} records his age as 43. This suggests he was born around 654, placing Amako no Iratsume's marriage prior to that「Munakata Taisha」『Place names of Fukuoka Prefecture』, Japanese Historical Place names Series 41, Heibonsha, 2004.. No burial goods identifying a specific individual have been excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun. However, considering its relationship with the nearby Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun and Miyajidake Cremation Tomb, a connection to the ancient Munakata clan is plausible{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == Miyajidake Cremation Tomb == The '''Miyajidake Cremation Tomb''' (みやじだけかそうぼ) is an ancient {{ill|Cremation tomb|ja|火葬墓|12=draft}} believed to have been located near the {{ill|Miyajidake Kofun|ja|宮地嶽古墳|12=draft}}. The tomb was discovered in [[1938]] (Shōwa 13) on the western slope of a hill (approx. 65 meters above sea level) east of the stone chamber’s entrance during reforestation work. A glass funerary urn was unearthed about one shaku (approx. 30 cm) beneath the surface{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The urn was placed inside a ceramic composite jar and contained a glass short-necked urn with a lid, which was encased in a bronze lidded pedestal jar{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Since the ceramics were from a later period, they are considered secondary burial items, and the original tomb's location and structure remain unknown{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The glass funerary urn is similar in design and manufacturing techniques to one found in the grave of {{ill|Fumi no Nemaro|ja|文祢麻呂|12=draft}} in {{ill|Uda City|ja|宇陀市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, which was dated to {{ill|Keiun|ja|慶雲|12=draft}} 4 (707). This suggests the Miyajidake Cremation Tomb was constructed in the early [[8th century]]{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Hypotheses regarding the buried individual include {{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘|12=draft}}, the daughter of {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|12=draft}}, or Munakata Tōjo, who is mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}} as having been appointed governor of Munakata District in [[Wadō|ja|和銅]] 2 (709){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The excavated funerary urn was designation1 a National Treasure in [[1961]] (Shōwa 36). == Historic site == === National Treasures === * burial goods Excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Kyushu National Museum (formerly in the Tokyo National Museum). Designated as a National Treasure on September 18, [[1936]], under the National Treasure Preservation Act; reclassified as Important Cultural Property under the [[Historic site Protection Law]] in [[1950]]; designation1 as a National Treasure on March 29, [[1952]]{{National Heritage Database|201|841|Miyajidake Kofun burial goods}}. * Glass Ossuary Excavated from the Grounds of Miyajidake Shrine (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Tokyo National Museum. Interior of the stone chamber |alternate_name=Maruzuka Kofun / Miyajidake Ōtsuka | part_of={{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft}} |location=[[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Fukutsu City]], Miyajimoto-cho 1241 (Ōtsuka) (within the grounds of {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft}}) | coordinates = 33 | coordinates = 46 | coordinates = 51.10 | coordinates = 130 | coordinates = 29 | coordinates = 19.15 | omitted = JP-40 | type={{ill|Round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} | area=Diameter: 35 meters | burial={{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}}-type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | burial goods=Gilded bronze-headed tachi swords, gilded bronze horse gear, gilded bronze crown, glass plates, bronze ware, and numerous burial items | Satellite Tombs= | built=Mid-7th century | Interred_individual=Possibly {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善|12=draft}} | Tomb Classification= | Historic Site=Part of the National Historic site "{{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft}}" | Historic Site=Burial items (National Treasure) | notes=Second-largest stone chamber in Japan | map=Japan Fukuoka | type=Round mound | map_dot_label=Miyajidake Kofun | map_dot_label=right }} '''Miyajidake Kofun''' (宮地嶽古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fukutsu City|ja|福津市|12=draft}}, [[Fukuoka Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the Kofuns comprising the {{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft}}, designation1 as a National Historic site. The burial items excavated from the mound are classified as a National Treasure. This kofun is known for having the second-largest stone chamber in Japan and for the discovery of numerous luxurious burial items. This article also includes information on the [[Miyajidake Kofun#Miyajidake Cremation Tomb|Miyajidake Cremation Tomb]], whose burial items are also designation1 as National Treasures. == Overview == [[File:Fudo Shrine (No.3 of Okunomiya 8 Shrines) in Miyajidake Shrine.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fudō Shrine (Okunomiya of Miyajidake Shrine)}}{{small|The hall of worship is built in front of the stone chamber opening.}}]] Miyajidake Kofun is a large circular Kofun constructed on the southern slope (approximately 55 meters above sea level) of Mount Miyajidake (elevation 180.7 meters) in northern Fukuoka Prefecture{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Nearby, ancient cremation graves associated with Miyajidake are believed to exist, and the surrounding area once featured small Kofuns. On a hill across the Misogi Pond, the {{ill|Miyaji Idenoue Kofun|ja|宮司井手ノ上古墳|12=draft}} is located{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Currently, the site is worshipped as Fudō Shrine, an Okunomiya (inner shrine) of Miyajidake Shrine. The stone chamber was opened in the mid-Edo period, and burial items were excavated multiple times during the Shōwa era. Measured surveys of the chamber were conducted in 1937 and 1996 (Shōwa 12 and Heisei 8), but no full excavation has been carried out. While the Kofun has been modified over time, it is estimated to have originally been a circular mound approximately 35 meters in diameter{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}}-type horizontal stone chamber, which opens to the east. The chamber, with a total length of 23 meters, is the second-largest of its kind in Japan. Though no excavations have been conducted inside the chamber, burial items believed to have originally been stored there have been discovered nearby, including a gilded bronze-headed tachi sword nearly 3 meters long, a gilded bronze crown, gilded bronze horse gear, glass plates, bronze ware, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}}. These burial goods are notable for their exceptional quality and quantity, and the horse gear and crown, adorned with arabesque patterns, reflect rich international influences. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the mid-7th century, during the {{ill|final stage of the Kofun period|ja|古墳時代終末期|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}} (or in the early to mid-7th century"Evaluation of the Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster > Miyajidake Kofun," *Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster III*, Fukutsu City Board of Education, 2013. / early 7th century{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, TK217-style period). It is widely regarded as the tomb of a leader from the Munakata clan, an ancient clan in the Munakata region. The specific interred individual is often identified as {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善|12=draft}}. The combination of the massive stone chamber and the luxurious burial items makes Miyajidake Kofun one of Japan's representative Kofuns. The burial site was designation1 a National Historic site in 2005 (Heisei 17), and its burial items were designation1 a National Treasure in 1952 (Shōwa 27). Access to the interior of the stone chamber is currently restricted except during the three annual grand festivals. == Archaeological History == * In the first year of the [[Kanpō]] era ([[1741]]), the stone chamber was exposed due to a landslide during heavy rain (as documented in the {{ill|Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel|ja|筑前国続風土記拾遺|12=draft}} compiled during the [[Tenpō]] era ([[1830]]–[[1844]])){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In the 4th year of the [[Enkyō]] era ([[1747]]), the deity Fudō Myōō was enshrined at the back of the stone chamber (as documented in the 'Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel'){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In [[1930]] (the 5th year of the [[Shōwa]] era), ancillary facilities were constructed around the tumulus in conjunction with the shrine's relocation{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1934]] (Shōwa 9), equestrian gear and swords were excavated during the construction of the shrine office{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On September 18, [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), the equestrian gear was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), an accurate survey of the stone chamber was conducted (by Kagayama Takeshi){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a glass ossuary was excavated during afforestation work on the eastern side of the tumulus{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On October 25, [[1939]] (Shōwa 14), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1951]] (Shōwa 26), fragments of a crown were excavated in front of the dromos{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. ** On March 29, [[1952]] (Shōwa 27), the excavated burial goods were designation1 as National Treasures (new Category). ** On April 27, [[1961]] (Shōwa 36), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (new Category). * In [[1996]] (Heisei 8), the stone chamber was resurveyed (by Ikenoue Hiroshi and others, reported in [[1999]]){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On March 2, [[2005]] (Heisei 17), it was designation1 as a [[Historic site]] of Japan as part of the "[[Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster]]"{{National Heritage Database|401|3422|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster}}. == Mound == [[File:Miyajidake-Kofun 20161014.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}{{small|Today, stone rows encircle the mound.}}]] The mound was built by cutting through the gentle slope of a ridge and reshaping the natural terrain{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The current mound has an elliptical type, measuring 27 meters north-south and 34 meters east-west, but it is estimated to have originally been a circular type with a diameter of about 35 meters{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A secondary layer of earth, approximately 2 meters thick, is observed on the mound, which is believed to be the soil excavated during the 1934 digging of the stone chamber{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Around the mound, rows of stones about 1 meter wide and 1.4 meters high encircle the structure, with three-tiered stacking near the dromos{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. These stone rows were installed before 1934 and are believed to have reduced the original size of the mound{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == burial == [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-1.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Bird's-eye view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Expanded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility is a {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber with a side entrance|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}} type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening towards the east. Among the passageway and main chamber, the rear section of the main chamber is slightly narrower, divided into a rear chamber and a front chamber, showcasing a multi-chamber structure similar to horizontal stone chambers in the Kinai region. The area of the stone chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}: * Total length of the stone chamber: Approx. 23.1 meters (current measurement: 23.5–24 meters) * Stone sarcophagus (rear chamber): Length 3.5 meters, width approx. 1.75 meters * Main chamber (front chamber): Length 11.7 meters, width 2.5–2.8 meters, height 2.2–3.1 meters ** Left niche (south niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.5 meters ** Right niche (north niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.3 meters The stone material for the chamber is said to be conglomerate rock from the Koi no Ura coast{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Large stones were used, suggesting significant labor was required to transport them from the coast to the mid-slope area{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. The stone chamber is the second largest nationwide after the {{ill|Maruyama Kofun (Kashihara)|ja|丸山古墳 (橿原市)|12=draft}} (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture), with a total length of 28.4 meters. In the stone sarcophagus (first stone from the rear), three approximately 3-meter monolithic stones are assembled. The main chamber (second to fourth stones from the rear) features monolithic stones, 3.1–4.5 meters in height, standing side by side on both sidewalls{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Particularly on the second stone from the rear, niches have been carved into both sides of the stone, which is the largest stone in the chamber, measuring more than 1.7 meters in thickness{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Historical records from the Edo period indicate that these niches existed from the beginning{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The passageway (fifth to seventh stones from the rear) is constructed with two to three layers of stacked stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Near the entrance, stones 0.3–0.4 meters in size are irregularly piled, considered to be secondary stonework{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The floor, currently covered with concrete, was likely originally paved with pebbles and arranged with floor stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The ceiling stones measure 0.5 meters thick in the sarcophagus area, 1 meter above the second stone (niche area), and 1.65 meters above the fourth stone{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A similar stone chamber structure to the Miyajidake Kofun is known from the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳|12=draft}} in Fukutsu City. Previously, the Miyajidake Kofun was thought to precede the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, but based on investigations from 2010–2011 (Heisei 22–23), it is now hypothesized that the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun predates the Miyajidake Kofun{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Reference: Bird's-eye view of the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳|12=draft}} stone chamber Miyajidake Kofun, sekkaku.jpg|Stone sarcophagus and main chamber (towards the rear wall)
{{small|The rear sarcophagus stone is the first stone. Niches are formed on the sidewalls of the second stone in the main chamber.}} Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-1.jpg|Main chamber (towards the rear wall) Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-2.jpg|Main chamber (towards the entrance) Miyajidake Kofun, entrance.jpg|Entrance area (towards the rear wall) == burial goods == [[File:HARNESS MIYAJIDAKE.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Gilt Bronze Stirrup (National Treasure)}}]] The grave goods excavated near the tumulus during the Shōwa period are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Items owned by Miyajidake Shrine (formerly stored in the Tokyo National Museum, later deposited in the Kyushu National Museum, and designation1 as National Treasures) are marked with an "M." * Swords ** Large gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 2.4–2.8 meters. Parts including the pommel, guard, sheath fittings, and blade remain. ** Gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 0.90 meters. Parts including the pommel, habaki fitting, sheath tip fitting, and blade remain. * Horse gear ** Gilt bronze saddle fittings (M) - Front and rear bridges are mostly intact, but most other fittings are missing. ** Gilt bronze stirrups (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze bridles with decorative plates (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze pendants (pair) (M) ** Saddle with arabesque fittings (M) ** Iron fittings (M) ** Various other fittings (7 items, gilt bronze saddle fittings included) (M) * Glass plates ** Three intact plates (M) - Possibly raw materials for glass beads. ** 27 fragments (M19, others: 8+) * Whetstone (M) * Openwork gilt bronze crown (M) * Glass beads (large, medium) - Total: 265 (M256, others: 6). Made of lead glass, semi-transparent green. * Gold rings - Total: 3 (M1, others: 2) * Copper bells - Total: 3 (M2, others: 1) * Copper nails - Total: 4 (M) * Decorative metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Other metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Copper chain - 1 unit (18 links) (M) * Copper vessels - Total: 2 (M). Includes one copper bowl with a lid and one tray. * Copper utility knife with sheath fittings (M) * [[Sue pottery]] - Total: 17 (M4, others: 13). Includes six bowls, five lids, two tall stemmed vessels, and one flat bottle. Older Sue pottery types (before the Oda IVA period, TK209 type) are excluded{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. * [[Haji pottery]] - Total: 3 (M). Includes one bowl and two jars. == Burial Individual ==
'''Genealogical chart based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}''' {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||01| 01={{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi|12=draft}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||!|}} {{familytree|border=0|01|~|y|~|02| 01=Ōama no Ōji
({{Supra|40}} {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft}})|02={{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘|12=draft}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||!}} {{familytree|border=0||||01| 01={{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子|12=draft}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The individual buried in the Miyajidake Kofun is unknown, but they are presumed to be a chief of the ancient Munakata clan (宗形氏/宗像氏) from the Munakata region. Specifically, one theory identifies the buried individual as '''{{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi|12=draft}}''' (むなかたのきみとくぜん). Munakata Tokuyoshi is believed to have been the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子|12=draft}} (654?–696). According to the genealogical records in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, in the second year of Emperor Tenmu (673), Prince Ōama (later {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft}}) married Amako no Iratsume, the daughter of Munakata Tokuyoshi, producing Prince Takechi. While details are sparse due to limited mentions in other texts, Prince Takechi played a central role as the commander-in-chief of Emperor Ōama's forces during the Jinshin War and was later appointed {{ill|Daijō-daijin|ja|太政大臣|12=draft}} in 690 under Empress Jitō. Munakata Tokuyoshi is therefore thought to have been instrumental in advancing the Munakata clan's influence within the central government「Munakata Tokuyoshi」『Dictionary of Ancient Japanese Clans, Popular Edition』, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2010.. Prince Takechi died in 696, with records in the {{ill|Kuge Bunin|ja|Kugyō補任|12=draft}} stating he was 42 or 43 years old, while the {{ill|Fusō Ryakki|ja|扶桑略記|12=draft}} records his age as 43. This suggests he was born around 654, placing Amako no Iratsume's marriage prior to that「Munakata Taisha」『Place names of Fukuoka Prefecture』, Japanese Historical Place names Series 41, Heibonsha, 2004.. No burial goods identifying a specific individual have been excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun. However, considering its relationship with the nearby Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun and Miyajidake Cremation Tomb, a connection to the ancient Munakata clan is plausible{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == Miyajidake Cremation Tomb == The '''Miyajidake Cremation Tomb''' (みやじだけかそうぼ) is an ancient {{ill|Cremation tomb|ja|火葬墓|12=draft}} believed to have been located near the {{ill|Miyajidake Kofun|ja|宮地嶽古墳|12=draft}}. The tomb was discovered in [[1938]] (Shōwa 13) on the western slope of a hill (approx. 65 meters above sea level) east of the stone chamber’s entrance during reforestation work. A glass funerary urn was unearthed about one shaku (approx. 30 cm) beneath the surface{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The urn was placed inside a ceramic composite jar and contained a glass short-necked urn with a lid, which was encased in a bronze lidded pedestal jar{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Since the ceramics were from a later period, they are considered secondary burial items, and the original tomb's location and structure remain unknown{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The glass funerary urn is similar in design and manufacturing techniques to one found in the grave of {{ill|Fumi no Nemaro|ja|文祢麻呂|12=draft}} in {{ill|Uda City|ja|宇陀市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, which was dated to {{ill|Keiun|ja|慶雲|12=draft}} 4 (707). This suggests the Miyajidake Cremation Tomb was constructed in the early [[8th century]]{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Hypotheses regarding the buried individual include {{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘|12=draft}}, the daughter of {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|12=draft}}, or Munakata Tōjo, who is mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}} as having been appointed governor of Munakata District in [[Wadō|ja|和銅]] 2 (709){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The excavated funerary urn was designation1 a National Treasure in [[1961]] (Shōwa 36). == Historic site == === National Treasures === * burial goods Excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Kyushu National Museum (formerly in the Tokyo National Museum). Designated as a National Treasure on September 18, [[1936]], under the National Treasure Preservation Act; reclassified as Important Cultural Property under the [[Historic site Protection Law]] in [[1950]]; designation1 as a National Treasure on March 29, [[1952]]{{National Heritage Database|201|841|Miyajidake Kofun burial goods}}. * Glass Ossuary Excavated from the Grounds of Miyajidake Shrine (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Tokyo National Museum. Designated as a National Treasure (former Category) on October 25, [[1939]], under the National Treasure Preservation Act; reclassified as Important Cultural Property under the Historic site Protection Law in 1950; designation1 as a National Treasure (new Category) on April 27, [[1961]]{{National Heritage Database|201|861|Glass Ossuary from Miyajidake Shrine}}. === Related Facilities === * [[Kyushu National Museum]] ([[Dazaifu City]], [[Fukuoka Prefecture]]) - Stores burial goods from the Miyajidake Kofun. * [[Tokyo National Museum]] ([[Taitō City]], [[Tokyo]]) - Stores burial goods from the Miyajidake Cremation Tomb. == notes == {{reflist}} == References == {{small|(References used in writing this article)}} * Site explanation board * Encyclopedias ** {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=Mori Teijirō|year=|chapter=Miyajidake Kofun|title=[[National History Dictionary (Shōwa Period)|国史大辞典]]|publisher=[[Yoshikawa Kōbunkan]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|Miyajidake Kofun (National History)|}}}} ** {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=Harada Michio|year=1989|chapter=Miyajidake Kofun|title=[[Japanese Kofun Dictionary]]|publisher=[[Tōkyōdō Publishing]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Miyajidake Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} ** {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=|year=2004|chapter=Miyajidake Kofun|title=Fukuoka Prefecture Place names|series=[[Japanese Historical Place names Series]] 41|publisher=[[Heibonsha]]|isbn=4582490417|ref={{Harvid|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}}} * Others ** {{Cite journal|language=ja|author=Ikenoue Hiroshi, Hanada Katsuhiro|title=Reexamination of the Miyajidake Kofun in Chikushi|date=1999-12|publisher=Japan Archaeological Society|journal=Archaeological Journal|volume=85|number=1|pages=19-56|url=|naid=|doi=|ref={{Harvid|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}}} ** {{Cite journal|language=ja|author=Kojima Atsushi|title={{PDFlink|[https://www.munakata-archives.asia/Dat/bunken/0000000047_01.pdf "Munakata-no-Kimi as Viewed from the End of Keyhole-shaped Tumuli"]}}|date=2018|publisher=Munakata-Okinoshima and Associated Heritage Sites World Heritage Promotion Council|journal=Okinoshima Studies|volume=|number=4|pages=19-40|url=|naid=|doi=|ref={{Harvid|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}}} - Link from "Munakata Archives," Munakata-Okinoshima and Associated Heritage Sites Preservation and Utilization Council. == Related Literature == {{small|(Related literature not used in writing this article)}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=Shimada Torajirō|year=1939|chapter=Regarding the Fudō Cave of the Miyajidake Kofun|title=[https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/84360 Historic sites, Scenic Spots, and Natural Monuments Survey Report]|volume=No. 13, Historic sites Section|publisher=Fukuoka Prefecture|isbn=|ref=}} - Link from the "Comprehensive Archaeological Report Database" by the Nara National Research Institute for Historic site. * {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=|year=1968|chapter=|title=Repair Report on the National Treasure burial goods Excavated from Miyajidake Kofun|publisher=Miyajidake Shrine|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=Oda Fujio|year=1982|chapter=Miyajidake Kofun|title=Exploring Japan's Kofun|volume=Western Japan Edition|publisher=Yūhikaku|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=|year=2022|chapter=|title=The World of Golden Treasures: National Treasure burial goods Excavated from Miyajidake Kofun (Special Exhibition for the 50th Anniversary of Ōnojo City's Municipal System)|publisher=Ōnojo Heart of the Homeland Museum|isbn=|ref=}} == See Also == * [[Miyajidake Shrine]] * {{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft}} ** [[Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun]] * [[Munakata Taisha]] == External Links == {{Commonscat|Miyajidake Kofun}} * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/841 Miyajidake Kofun burial goods], [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/861 Glass Ossuary from Miyajidake Shrine Grounds] - National Historic site Database (Agency for Cultural Affairs) * [https://www.fukuoka-bunkazai.jp/frmDetail.aspx?db=1&id=45 Miyajidake Kofun burial goods] - "Fukuoka's Historic site," Fukuoka Prefecture Education and Historic site Division [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[sn:Miyajidake Kofun]][[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[sn:Miyajidake Kofun]]{{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)]] [[Category:Historic sites of Japan]] [[Category:Kofuns in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Burial practices in Japan]] [[Category:Kofun period]] [[Category:Miyajidake Kofun]] [[Category:Cremation]] [[Category:Burial sites in Japan]] [[Category:National Treasures of Japan]] [[Category:Historic sites in Japan]] [[Category:History of Fukutsu City]] [[Category:Round Kofun]] [[Category:National Treasures of Japan (Archaeological and Historical Materials)]] [[Category:National Treasures in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:National Historic sites in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Munakata clan|Tomb]] [[Category:Completion tier 3]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:円墳]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Completion tier 3]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] }} [[ja:宮地嶽古墳]] [[ja:宮地嶽火葬墓]] [[sn:Miyajidake Kofun]] [[en:Miyajidake Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] {{Kofun navbar}}

Interior of the stone chamber |alternate_name=Maruzuka Kofun / Miyajidake Ōtsuka | part_of={{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} |location=[[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Fukutsu City]], Miyajimoto-cho 1241 (Ōtsuka) (within the grounds of {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}}) | coordinates = 33 | coordinates = 46 | coordinates = 51.10 | coordinates = 130 | coordinates = 29 | coordinates = 19.15 | omitted = JP-40 | type={{ill|Round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} | area=Diameter: 35 meters | burial={{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}-type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} | burial goods=Gilded bronze-headed tachi swords, gilded bronze horse gear, gilded bronze crown, glass plates, bronze ware, and numerous burial items | Satellite Tombs= | built=Mid-7th century | Interred_individual=Possibly {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善|12=draft|12=draft}} | Tomb Classification= | Historic Site=Part of the National Historic site "{{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}" | Historic Site=Burial items (National Treasure) | notes=Second-largest stone chamber in Japan | map=Japan Fukuoka | type=Round mound | map_dot_label=Miyajidake Kofun | map_dot_label=right }} '''Miyajidake Kofun''' (宮地嶽古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fukutsu City|ja|福津市|12=draft|12=draft}}, [[Fukuoka Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and one of the Kofuns comprising the {{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, designation1 as a National Historic site. The burial items excavated from the mound are classified as a National Treasure. This kofun is known for having the second-largest stone chamber in Japan and for the discovery of numerous luxurious burial items. This article also includes information on the [[Miyajidake Kofun#Miyajidake Cremation Tomb|Miyajidake Cremation Tomb]], whose burial items are also designation1 as National Treasures. == Overview == [[File:Fudo Shrine (No.3 of Okunomiya 8 Shrines) in Miyajidake Shrine.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fudō Shrine (Okunomiya of Miyajidake Shrine)}}{{small|The hall of worship is built in front of the stone chamber opening.}}]] Miyajidake Kofun is a large circular Kofun constructed on the southern slope (approximately 55 meters above sea level) of Mount Miyajidake (elevation 180.7 meters) in northern Fukuoka Prefecture{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Nearby, ancient cremation graves associated with Miyajidake are believed to exist, and the surrounding area once featured small Kofuns. On a hill across the Misogi Pond, the {{ill|Miyaji Idenoue Kofun|ja|宮司井手ノ上古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} is located{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Currently, the site is worshipped as Fudō Shrine, an Okunomiya (inner shrine) of Miyajidake Shrine. The stone chamber was opened in the mid-Edo period, and burial items were excavated multiple times during the Shōwa era. Measured surveys of the chamber were conducted in 1937 and 1996 (Shōwa 12 and Heisei 8), but no full excavation has been carried out. While the Kofun has been modified over time, it is estimated to have originally been a circular mound approximately 35 meters in diameter{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}-type horizontal stone chamber, which opens to the east. The chamber, with a total length of 23 meters, is the second-largest of its kind in Japan. Though no excavations have been conducted inside the chamber, burial items believed to have originally been stored there have been discovered nearby, including a gilded bronze-headed tachi sword nearly 3 meters long, a gilded bronze crown, gilded bronze horse gear, glass plates, bronze ware, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}. These burial goods are notable for their exceptional quality and quantity, and the horse gear and crown, adorned with arabesque patterns, reflect rich international influences. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the mid-7th century, during the {{ill|final stage of the Kofun period|ja|古墳時代終末期|12=draft|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}} (or in the early to mid-7th century"Evaluation of the Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster > Miyajidake Kofun," *Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster III*, Fukutsu City Board of Education, 2013. / early 7th century{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, TK217-style period). It is widely regarded as the tomb of a leader from the Munakata clan, an ancient clan in the Munakata region. The specific interred individual is often identified as {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善|12=draft|12=draft}}. The combination of the massive stone chamber and the luxurious burial items makes Miyajidake Kofun one of Japan's representative Kofuns. The burial site was designation1 a National Historic site in 2005 (Heisei 17), and its burial items were designation1 a National Treasure in 1952 (Shōwa 27). Access to the interior of the stone chamber is currently restricted except during the three annual grand festivals. == Archaeological History == * In the first year of the [[Kanpō]] era ([[1741]]), the stone chamber was exposed due to a landslide during heavy rain (as documented in the {{ill|Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel|ja|筑前国続風土記拾遺|12=draft|12=draft}} compiled during the [[Tenpō]] era ([[1830]]–[[1844]])){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In the 4th year of the [[Enkyō]] era ([[1747]]), the deity Fudō Myōō was enshrined at the back of the stone chamber (as documented in the 'Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel'){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In [[1930]] (the 5th year of the [[Shōwa]] era), ancillary facilities were constructed around the tumulus in conjunction with the shrine's relocation{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1934]] (Shōwa 9), equestrian gear and swords were excavated during the construction of the shrine office{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On September 18, [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), the equestrian gear was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), an accurate survey of the stone chamber was conducted (by Kagayama Takeshi){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a glass ossuary was excavated during afforestation work on the eastern side of the tumulus{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On October 25, [[1939]] (Shōwa 14), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1951]] (Shōwa 26), fragments of a crown were excavated in front of the dromos{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. ** On March 29, [[1952]] (Shōwa 27), the excavated burial goods were designation1 as National Treasures (new Category). ** On April 27, [[1961]] (Shōwa 36), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (new Category). * In [[1996]] (Heisei 8), the stone chamber was resurveyed (by Ikenoue Hiroshi and others, reported in [[1999]]){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On March 2, [[2005]] (Heisei 17), it was designation1 as a [[Historic site]] of Japan as part of the "[[Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster]]"{{National Heritage Database|401|3422|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster}}. == Mound == [[File:Miyajidake-Kofun 20161014.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}{{small|Today, stone rows encircle the mound.}}]] The mound was built by cutting through the gentle slope of a ridge and reshaping the natural terrain{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The current mound has an elliptical type, measuring 27 meters north-south and 34 meters east-west, but it is estimated to have originally been a circular type with a diameter of about 35 meters{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A secondary layer of earth, approximately 2 meters thick, is observed on the mound, which is believed to be the soil excavated during the 1934 digging of the stone chamber{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Around the mound, rows of stones about 1 meter wide and 1.4 meters high encircle the structure, with three-tiered stacking near the dromos{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. These stone rows were installed before 1934 and are believed to have reduced the original size of the mound{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == burial == [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-1.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Bird's-eye view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Expanded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility is a {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber with a side entrance|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening towards the east. Among the passageway and main chamber, the rear section of the main chamber is slightly narrower, divided into a rear chamber and a front chamber, showcasing a multi-chamber structure similar to horizontal stone chambers in the Kinai region. The area of the stone chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}: * Total length of the stone chamber: Approx. 23.1 meters (current measurement: 23.5–24 meters) * Stone sarcophagus (rear chamber): Length 3.5 meters, width approx. 1.75 meters * Main chamber (front chamber): Length 11.7 meters, width 2.5–2.8 meters, height 2.2–3.1 meters ** Left niche (south niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.5 meters ** Right niche (north niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.3 meters The stone material for the chamber is said to be conglomerate rock from the Koi no Ura coast{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Large stones were used, suggesting significant labor was required to transport them from the coast to the mid-slope area{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. The stone chamber is the second largest nationwide after the {{ill|Maruyama Kofun (Kashihara)|ja|丸山古墳 (橿原市)|12=draft|12=draft}} (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture), with a total length of 28.4 meters. In the stone sarcophagus (first stone from the rear), three approximately 3-meter monolithic stones are assembled. The main chamber (second to fourth stones from the rear) features monolithic stones, 3.1–4.5 meters in height, standing side by side on both sidewalls{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Particularly on the second stone from the rear, niches have been carved into both sides of the stone, which is the largest stone in the chamber, measuring more than 1.7 meters in thickness{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Historical records from the Edo period indicate that these niches existed from the beginning{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The passageway (fifth to seventh stones from the rear) is constructed with two to three layers of stacked stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Near the entrance, stones 0.3–0.4 meters in size are irregularly piled, considered to be secondary stonework{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The floor, currently covered with concrete, was likely originally paved with pebbles and arranged with floor stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The ceiling stones measure 0.5 meters thick in the sarcophagus area, 1 meter above the second stone (niche area), and 1.65 meters above the fourth stone{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A similar stone chamber structure to the Miyajidake Kofun is known from the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in Fukutsu City. Previously, the Miyajidake Kofun was thought to precede the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, but based on investigations from 2010–2011 (Heisei 22–23), it is now hypothesized that the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun predates the Miyajidake Kofun{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Reference: Bird's-eye view of the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} stone chamber Miyajidake Kofun, sekkaku.jpg|Stone sarcophagus and main chamber (towards the rear wall)
{{small|The rear sarcophagus stone is the first stone. Niches are formed on the sidewalls of the second stone in the main chamber.}} Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-1.jpg|Main chamber (towards the rear wall) Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-2.jpg|Main chamber (towards the entrance) Miyajidake Kofun, entrance.jpg|Entrance area (towards the rear wall) == burial goods == [[File:HARNESS MIYAJIDAKE.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Gilt Bronze Stirrup (National Treasure)}}]] The grave goods excavated near the tumulus during the Shōwa period are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Items owned by Miyajidake Shrine (formerly stored in the Tokyo National Museum, later deposited in the Kyushu National Museum, and designation1 as National Treasures) are marked with an "M." * Swords ** Large gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 2.4–2.8 meters. Parts including the pommel, guard, sheath fittings, and blade remain. ** Gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 0.90 meters. Parts including the pommel, habaki fitting, sheath tip fitting, and blade remain. * Horse gear ** Gilt bronze saddle fittings (M) - Front and rear bridges are mostly intact, but most other fittings are missing. ** Gilt bronze stirrups (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze bridles with decorative plates (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze pendants (pair) (M) ** Saddle with arabesque fittings (M) ** Iron fittings (M) ** Various other fittings (7 items, gilt bronze saddle fittings included) (M) * Glass plates ** Three intact plates (M) - Possibly raw materials for glass beads. ** 27 fragments (M19, others: 8+) * Whetstone (M) * Openwork gilt bronze crown (M) * Glass beads (large, medium) - Total: 265 (M256, others: 6). Made of lead glass, semi-transparent green. * Gold rings - Total: 3 (M1, others: 2) * Copper bells - Total: 3 (M2, others: 1) * Copper nails - Total: 4 (M) * Decorative metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Other metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Copper chain - 1 unit (18 links) (M) * Copper vessels - Total: 2 (M). Includes one copper bowl with a lid and one tray. * Copper utility knife with sheath fittings (M) * [[Sue pottery]] - Total: 17 (M4, others: 13). Includes six bowls, five lids, two tall stemmed vessels, and one flat bottle. Older Sue pottery types (before the Oda IVA period, TK209 type) are excluded{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. * [[Haji pottery]] - Total: 3 (M). Includes one bowl and two jars. == Burial Individual ==
'''Genealogical chart based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft|12=draft}}''' {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||01| 01={{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi|12=draft|12=draft}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||!|}} {{familytree|border=0|01|~|y|~|02| 01=Ōama no Ōji
({{Supra|40}} {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft|12=draft}})|02={{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘|12=draft|12=draft}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||!}} {{familytree|border=0||||01| 01={{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子|12=draft|12=draft}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The individual buried in the Miyajidake Kofun is unknown, but they are presumed to be a chief of the ancient Munakata clan (宗形氏/宗像氏) from the Munakata region. Specifically, one theory identifies the buried individual as '''{{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (むなかたのきみとくぜん). Munakata Tokuyoshi is believed to have been the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子|12=draft|12=draft}} (654?–696). According to the genealogical records in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft|12=draft}}, in the second year of Emperor Tenmu (673), Prince Ōama (later {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft|12=draft}}) married Amako no Iratsume, the daughter of Munakata Tokuyoshi, producing Prince Takechi. While details are sparse due to limited mentions in other texts, Prince Takechi played a central role as the commander-in-chief of Emperor Ōama's forces during the Jinshin War and was later appointed {{ill|Daijō-daijin|ja|太政大臣|12=draft|12=draft}} in 690 under Empress Jitō. Munakata Tokuyoshi is therefore thought to have been instrumental in advancing the Munakata clan's influence within the central government「Munakata Tokuyoshi」『Dictionary of Ancient Japanese Clans, Popular Edition』, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2010.. Prince Takechi died in 696, with records in the {{ill|Kuge Bunin|ja|Kugyō補任|12=draft|12=draft}} stating he was 42 or 43 years old, while the {{ill|Fusō Ryakki|ja|扶桑略記|12=draft|12=draft}} records his age as 43. This suggests he was born around 654, placing Amako no Iratsume's marriage prior to that「Munakata Taisha」『Place names of Fukuoka Prefecture』, Japanese Historical Place names Series 41, Heibonsha, 2004.. No burial goods identifying a specific individual have been excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun. However, considering its relationship with the nearby Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun and Miyajidake Cremation Tomb, a connection to the ancient Munakata clan is plausible{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == Miyajidake Cremation Tomb == The '''Miyajidake Cremation Tomb''' (みやじだけかそうぼ) is an ancient {{ill|Cremation tomb|ja|火葬墓|12=draft|12=draft}} believed to have been located near the {{ill|Miyajidake Kofun|ja|宮地嶽古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. The tomb was discovered in [[1938]] (Shōwa 13) on the western slope of a hill (approx. 65 meters above sea level) east of the stone chamber’s entrance during reforestation work. A glass funerary urn was unearthed about one shaku (approx. 30 cm) beneath the surface{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The urn was placed inside a ceramic composite jar and contained a glass short-necked urn with a lid, which was encased in a bronze lidded pedestal jar{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Since the ceramics were from a later period, they are considered secondary burial items, and the original tomb's location and structure remain unknown{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The glass funerary urn is similar in design and manufacturing techniques to one found in the grave of {{ill|Fumi no Nemaro|ja|文祢麻呂|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Uda City|ja|宇陀市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, which was dated to {{ill|Keiun|ja|慶雲|12=draft|12=draft}} 4 (707). This suggests the Miyajidake Cremation Tomb was constructed in the early [[8th century]]{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Hypotheses regarding the buried individual include {{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘|12=draft|12=draft}}, the daughter of {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|12=draft|12=draft}}, or Munakata Tōjo, who is mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft|12=draft}} as having been appointed governor of Munakata District in [[Wadō|ja|和銅]] 2 (709){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The excavated funerary urn was designation1 a National Treasure in [[1961]] (Shōwa 36). == Historic site == === National Treasures === * burial goods Excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Kyushu National Museum (formerly in the Tokyo National Museum). Designated as a National Treasure on September 18, [[1936]], under the National Treasure Preservation Act; reclassified as Important Cultural Property under the [[Historic site Protection Law]] in [[1950]]; designation1 as a National Treasure on March 29, [[1952]]{{National Heritage Database|201|841|Miyajidake Kofun burial goods}}. * Glass Ossuary Excavated from the Grounds of Miyajidake Shrine (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Tokyo National Museum. It is a {{ill|round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and one of the Kofuns comprising the {{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, designation1 as a National Historic site. The burial items excavated from the mound are classified as a National Treasure. This kofun is known for having the second-largest stone chamber in Japan and for the discovery of numerous luxurious burial items. This article also includes information on the [[Miyajidake Kofun#Miyajidake Cremation Tomb|Miyajidake Cremation Tomb]], whose burial items are also designation1 as National Treasures. == Overview == [[File:Fudo Shrine (No.3 of Okunomiya 8 Shrines) in Miyajidake Shrine.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fudō Shrine (Okunomiya of Miyajidake Shrine)}}{{small|The hall of worship is built in front of the stone chamber opening.}}]] Miyajidake Kofun is a large circular Kofun constructed on the southern slope (approximately 55 meters above sea level) of Mount Miyajidake (elevation 180.7 meters) in northern Fukuoka Prefecture{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Nearby, ancient cremation graves associated with Miyajidake are believed to exist, and the surrounding area once featured small Kofuns. On a hill across the Misogi Pond, the {{ill|Miyaji Idenoue Kofun|ja|宮司井手ノ上古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} is located{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Currently, the site is worshipped as Fudō Shrine, an Okunomiya (inner shrine) of Miyajidake Shrine. The stone chamber was opened in the mid-Edo period, and burial items were excavated multiple times during the Shōwa era. Measured surveys of the chamber were conducted in 1937 and 1996 (Shōwa 12 and Heisei 8), but no full excavation has been carried out. While the Kofun has been modified over time, it is estimated to have originally been a circular mound approximately 35 meters in diameter{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}-type horizontal stone chamber, which opens to the east. The chamber, with a total length of 23 meters, is the second-largest of its kind in Japan. Though no excavations have been conducted inside the chamber, burial items believed to have originally been stored there have been discovered nearby, including a gilded bronze-headed tachi sword nearly 3 meters long, a gilded bronze crown, gilded bronze horse gear, glass plates, bronze ware, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}. These burial goods are notable for their exceptional quality and quantity, and the horse gear and crown, adorned with arabesque patterns, reflect rich international influences. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the mid-7th century, during the {{ill|final stage of the Kofun period|ja|古墳時代終末期|12=draft|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}} (or in the early to mid-7th century"Evaluation of the Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster > Miyajidake Kofun," *Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster III*, Fukutsu City Board of Education, 2013. / early 7th century{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, TK217-style period). It is widely regarded as the tomb of a leader from the Munakata clan, an ancient clan in the Munakata region. The specific interred individual is often identified as {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善|12=draft|12=draft}}. The combination of the massive stone chamber and the luxurious burial items makes Miyajidake Kofun one of Japan's representative Kofuns. The burial site was designation1 a National Historic site in 2005 (Heisei 17), and its burial items were designation1 a National Treasure in 1952 (Shōwa 27). Access to the interior of the stone chamber is currently restricted except during the three annual grand festivals. == Archaeological History == * In the first year of the [[Kanpō]] era ([[1741]]), the stone chamber was exposed due to a landslide during heavy rain (as documented in the {{ill|Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel|ja|筑前国続風土記拾遺|12=draft|12=draft}} compiled during the [[Tenpō]] era ([[1830]]–[[1844]])){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In the 4th year of the [[Enkyō]] era ([[1747]]), the deity Fudō Myōō was enshrined at the back of the stone chamber (as documented in the 'Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel'){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In [[1930]] (the 5th year of the [[Shōwa]] era), ancillary facilities were constructed around the tumulus in conjunction with the shrine's relocation{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1934]] (Shōwa 9), equestrian gear and swords were excavated during the construction of the shrine Database|401|3422|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster}}. == Mound == [[File:Miyajidake-Kofun 20161014.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}{{small|Today, stone rows encircle the mound.}}]] The mound was built by cutting through the gentle slope of a ridge and reshaping the natural terrain{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The current mound has an elliptical type, measuring 27 meters north-south and 34 meters east-west, but it is estimated to have originally been a circular type with a diameter of about 35 meters{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A secondary layer of earth, approximately 2 meters thick, is observed on the mound, which is believed to be the soil excavated during the 1934 digging of the stone chamber{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Around the mound, rows of stones about 1 meter wide and 1.4 meters high encircle the structure, with three-tiered stacking near the dromos{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. These stone rows were installed before 1934 and are believed to have reduced the original size of the mound{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == burial == [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-1.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Bird's-eye view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Expanded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility is a {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber with a side entrance|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening towards the east. Among the passageway and main chamber, the rear section of the main chamber is slightly narrower, divided into a rear chamber and a front chamber, showcasing a multi-chamber structure similar to horizontal stone chambers in the Kinai region. The area of the stone chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}: * Total length of the stone chamber: Approx. 23.1 meters (current measurement: 23.5–24 meters) * Stone sarcophagus (rear chamber): Length 3.5 meters, width approx. 1.75 meters * Main chamber (front chamber): Length 11.7 meters, width 2.5–2.8 meters, height 2.2–3.1 meters ** Left niche (south niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.5 meters ** Right niche (north niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.3 meters The stone material for the chamber is said to be conglomerate rock from the Koi no Ura coast{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Large stones were used, suggesting significant labor was required to transport them from the coast to the mid-slope area{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. The stone chamber is the second largest nationwide after the {{ill|Maruyama Kofun (Kashihara)|ja|丸山古墳 (橿原市)|12=draft|12=draft}} (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture), with a total length of 28.4 meters. In the stone sarcophagus (first stone from the rear), three approximately 3-meter monolithic stones are assembled. The main chamber (second to fourth stones from the rear) features monolithic stones, 3.1–4.5 meters in height, standing side by side on both sidewalls{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Particularly on the second stone from the rear, niches have been carved into both sides of the stone, which is the largest stone in the chamber, measuring more than 1.7 meters in thickness{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Historical records from the Edo period indicate that these niches existed from the beginning{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The passageway (fifth to seventh stones from the rear) is constructed with two to three layers of stacked stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Near the entrance, stones 0.3–0.4 meters in size are irregularly piled, considered to be secondary stonework{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The floor, currently covered with concrete, was likely originally paved with pebbles and arranged with floor stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The ceiling stones measure 0.5 meters thick in the sarcophagus area, 1 meter above the second stone (niche area), and 1.65 meters above the fourth stone{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A similar stone chamber structure to the Miyajidake Kofun is known from the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in Fukutsu City. Previously, the Miyajidake Kofun was thought to precede the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, but based on investigations from 2010–2011 (Heisei 22–23), it is now hypothesized that the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun predates the Miyajidake Kofun{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. Items owned by Miyajidake Shrine (formerly stored in the Tokyo National Museum, later deposited in the Kyushu National Museum, and designation1 as National Treasures) are marked with an "M." * Swords ** Large gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 2.4–2.8 meters. Parts including the pommel, guard, sheath fittings, and blade remain. ** Gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 0.90 meters. Parts including the pommel, habaki fitting, sheath tip fitting, and blade remain. * Horse gear ** Gilt bronze saddle fittings (M) - Front and rear bridges are mostly intact, but most other fittings are missing. ** Gilt bronze stirrups (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze bridles with decorative plates (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze pendants (pair) (M) ** Saddle with arabesque fittings (M) ** Iron fittings (M) ** Various other fittings (7 items, gilt bronze saddle fittings included) (M) * Glass plates ** Three intact plates (M) - Possibly raw materials for glass beads. ** 27 fragments (M19, others: 8+) * Whetstone (M) * Openwork gilt bronze crown (M) * Glass beads (large, medium) - Total: 265 (M256, others: 6). Made of lead glass, semi-transparent green. * Gold rings - Total: 3 (M1, others: 2) * Copper bells - Total: 3 (M2, others: 1) * Copper nails - Total: 4 (M) * Decorative metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Other metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Copper chain - 1 unit (18 links) (M) * Copper vessels - Total: 2 (M). Includes one copper bowl with a lid and one tray. * Copper utility knife with sheath fittings (M) * [[Sue pottery]] - Total: 17 (M4, others: 13). Includes six bowls, five lids, two tall stemmed vessels, and one flat bottle. Older Sue pottery types (before the Oda IVA period, TK209 type) are excluded{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. * [[Haji pottery]] - Total: 3 (M). Includes one bowl and two jars. == Burial Individual ==
