Interior of the stone chamber |alternate_name=Maruzuka Kofun / Miyajidake Ōtsuka | part_of={{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群}} |location=[[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Fukutsu City]], Miyajimoto-cho 1241 (Ōtsuka) (within the grounds of {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社}}) | coordinates = 33 | coordinates = 46 | coordinates = 51.10 | coordinates = 130 | coordinates = 29 | coordinates = 19.15 | omitted = JP-40 | type={{ill|Round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} | area=Diameter: 35 meters | burial={{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}-type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | burial goods=Gilded bronze-headed tachi swords, gilded bronze horse gear, gilded bronze crown, glass plates, bronze ware, and numerous burial items | Satellite Tombs= | built=Mid-7th century | Interred_individual=Possibly {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善}} | Tomb Classification= | Historic Site=Part of the National Historic site "{{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群}}" | Historic Site=Burial items (National Treasure) | notes=Second-largest stone chamber in Japan | map=Japan Fukuoka | type=Round mound | map_dot_label=Miyajidake Kofun | map_dot_label=right }} '''Miyajidake Kofun''' (宮地嶽古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fukutsu City|ja|福津市}}, [[Fukuoka Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the Kofuns comprising the {{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群}}, designation1 as a National Historic site. The burial items excavated from the mound are classified as a National Treasure. This kofun is known for having the second-largest stone chamber in Japan and for the discovery of numerous luxurious burial items. This article also includes information on the [[Miyajidake Kofun#Miyajidake Cremation Tomb|Miyajidake Cremation Tomb]], whose burial items are also designation1 as National Treasures. == Overview == [[File:Fudo Shrine (No.3 of Okunomiya 8 Shrines) in Miyajidake Shrine.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fudō Shrine (Okunomiya of Miyajidake Shrine)}}{{small|The hall of worship is built in front of the stone chamber opening.}}]] Miyajidake Kofun is a large circular Kofun constructed on the southern slope (approximately 55 meters above sea level) of Mount Miyajidake (elevation 180.7 meters) in northern Fukuoka Prefecture{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Nearby, ancient cremation graves associated with Miyajidake are believed to exist, and the surrounding area once featured small Kofuns. On a hill across the Misogi Pond, the {{ill|Miyaji Idenoue Kofun|ja|宮司井手ノ上古墳}} is located{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Currently, the site is worshipped as Fudō Shrine, an Okunomiya (inner shrine) of Miyajidake Shrine. The stone chamber was opened in the mid-Edo period, and burial items were excavated multiple times during the Shōwa era. Measured surveys of the chamber were conducted in 1937 and 1996 (Shōwa 12 and Heisei 8), but no full excavation has been carried out. While the Kofun has been modified over time, it is estimated to have originally been a circular mound approximately 35 meters in diameter{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}-type horizontal stone chamber, which opens to the east. The chamber, with a total length of 23 meters, is the second-largest of its kind in Japan. Though no excavations have been conducted inside the chamber, burial items believed to have originally been stored there have been discovered nearby, including a gilded bronze-headed tachi sword nearly 3 meters long, a gilded bronze crown, gilded bronze horse gear, glass plates, bronze ware, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}. These burial goods are notable for their exceptional quality and quantity, and the horse gear and crown, adorned with arabesque patterns, reflect rich international influences. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the mid-7th century, during the {{ill|final stage of the Kofun period|ja|古墳時代終末期}}{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}} (or in the early to mid-7th century"Evaluation of the Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster > Miyajidake Kofun," *Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster III*, Fukutsu City Board of Education, 2013. / early 7th century{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, TK217-style period). It is widely regarded as the tomb of a leader from the Munakata clan, an ancient clan in the Munakata region. The specific interred individual is often identified as {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善}}. The combination of the massive stone chamber and the luxurious burial items makes Miyajidake Kofun one of Japan's representative Kofuns. The burial site was designation1 a National Historic site in 2005 (Heisei 17), and its burial items were designation1 a National Treasure in 1952 (Shōwa 27). Access to the interior of the stone chamber is currently restricted except during the three annual grand festivals. == Archaeological History == * In the first year of the [[Kanpō]] era ([[1741]]), the stone chamber was exposed due to a landslide during heavy rain (as documented in the {{ill|Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel|ja|筑前国続風土記拾遺}} compiled during the [[Tenpō]] era ([[1830]]–[[1844]])){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In the 4th year of the [[Enkyō]] era ([[1747]]), the deity Fudō Myōō was enshrined at the back of the stone chamber (as documented in the 'Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel'){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In [[1930]] (the 5th year of the [[Shōwa]] era), ancillary facilities were constructed around the tumulus in conjunction with the shrine's relocation{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1934]] (Shōwa 9), equestrian gear and swords were excavated during the construction of the shrine office{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On September 18, [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), the equestrian gear was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), an accurate survey of the stone chamber was conducted (by Kagayama Takeshi){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a glass ossuary was excavated during afforestation work on the eastern side of the tumulus{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On October 25, [[1939]] (Shōwa 14), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1951]] (Shōwa 26), fragments of a crown were excavated in front of the dromos{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. ** On March 29, [[1952]] (Shōwa 27), the excavated burial goods were designation1 as National Treasures (new Category). ** On April 27, [[1961]] (Shōwa 36), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (new Category). * In [[1996]] (Heisei 8), the stone chamber was resurveyed (by Ikenoue Hiroshi and others, reported in [[1999]]){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On March 2, [[2005]] (Heisei 17), it was designation1 as a [[Historic site]] of Japan as part of the "[[Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster]]"{{National Heritage Database|401|3422|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster}}. == Mound == [[File:Miyajidake-Kofun 20161014.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}{{small|Today, stone rows encircle the mound.}}]] The mound was built by cutting through the gentle slope of a ridge and reshaping the natural terrain{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The current mound has an elliptical type, measuring 27 meters north-south and 34 meters east-west, but it is estimated to have originally been a circular type with a diameter of about 35 meters{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A secondary layer of earth, approximately 2 meters thick, is observed on the mound, which is believed to be the soil excavated during the 1934 digging of the stone chamber{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Around the mound, rows of stones about 1 meter wide and 1.4 meters high encircle the structure, with three-tiered stacking near the dromos{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. These stone rows were installed before 1934 and are believed to have reduced the original size of the mound{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == burial == [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-1.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Bird's-eye view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Expanded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility is a {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber with a side entrance|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}} type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening towards the east. Among the passageway and main chamber, the rear section of the main chamber is slightly narrower, divided into a rear chamber and a front chamber, showcasing a multi-chamber structure similar to horizontal stone chambers in the Kinai region. The area of the stone chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}: * Total length of the stone chamber: Approx. 23.1 meters (current measurement: 23.5–24 meters) * Stone sarcophagus (rear chamber): Length 3.5 meters, width approx. 1.75 meters * Main chamber (front chamber): Length 11.7 meters, width 2.5–2.8 meters, height 2.2–3.1 meters ** Left niche (south niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.5 meters ** Right niche (north niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.3 meters The stone material for the chamber is said to be conglomerate rock from the Koi no Ura coast{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Large stones were used, suggesting significant labor was required to transport them from the coast to the mid-slope area{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. The stone chamber is the second largest nationwide after the {{ill|Maruyama Kofun (Kashihara)|ja|丸山古墳 (橿原市)}} (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture), with a total length of 28.4 meters. In the stone sarcophagus (first stone from the rear), three approximately 3-meter monolithic stones are assembled. The main chamber (second to fourth stones from the rear) features monolithic stones, 3.1–4.5 meters in height, standing side by side on both sidewalls{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Particularly on the second stone from the rear, niches have been carved into both sides of the stone, which is the largest stone in the chamber, measuring more than 1.7 meters in thickness{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Historical records from the Edo period indicate that these niches existed from the beginning{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The passageway (fifth to seventh stones from the rear) is constructed with two to three layers of stacked stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Near the entrance, stones 0.3–0.4 meters in size are irregularly piled, considered to be secondary stonework{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The floor, currently covered with concrete, was likely originally paved with pebbles and arranged with floor stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The ceiling stones measure 0.5 meters thick in the sarcophagus area, 1 meter above the second stone (niche area), and 1.65 meters above the fourth stone{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A similar stone chamber structure to the Miyajidake Kofun is known from the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳}} in Fukutsu City. Previously, the Miyajidake Kofun was thought to precede the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, but based on investigations from 2010–2011 (Heisei 22–23), it is now hypothesized that the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun predates the Miyajidake Kofun{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Reference: Bird's-eye view of the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳}} stone chamber Miyajidake Kofun, sekkaku.jpg|Stone sarcophagus and main chamber (towards the rear wall)
{{small|The rear sarcophagus stone is the first stone. Niches are formed on the sidewalls of the second stone in the main chamber.}} Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-1.jpg|Main chamber (towards the rear wall) Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-2.jpg|Main chamber (towards the entrance) Miyajidake Kofun, entrance.jpg|Entrance area (towards the rear wall) == burial goods == [[File:HARNESS MIYAJIDAKE.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Gilt Bronze Stirrup (National Treasure)}}]] The grave goods excavated near the tumulus during the Shōwa period are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Items owned by Miyajidake Shrine (formerly stored in the Tokyo National Museum, later deposited in the Kyushu National Museum, and designation1 as National Treasures) are marked with an "M." * Swords ** Large gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 2.4–2.8 meters. Parts including the pommel, guard, sheath fittings, and blade remain. ** Gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 0.90 meters. Parts including the pommel, habaki fitting, sheath tip fitting, and blade remain. * Horse gear ** Gilt bronze saddle fittings (M) - Front and rear bridges are mostly intact, but most other fittings are missing. ** Gilt bronze stirrups (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze bridles with decorative plates (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze pendants (pair) (M) ** Saddle with arabesque fittings (M) ** Iron fittings (M) ** Various other fittings (7 items, gilt bronze saddle fittings included) (M) * Glass plates ** Three intact plates (M) - Possibly raw materials for glass beads. ** 27 fragments (M19, others: 8+) * Whetstone (M) * Openwork gilt bronze crown (M) * Glass beads (large, medium) - Total: 265 (M256, others: 6). Made of lead glass, semi-transparent green. * Gold rings - Total: 3 (M1, others: 2) * Copper bells - Total: 3 (M2, others: 1) * Copper nails - Total: 4 (M) * Decorative metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Other metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Copper chain - 1 unit (18 links) (M) * Copper vessels - Total: 2 (M). Includes one copper bowl with a lid and one tray. * Copper utility knife with sheath fittings (M) * [[Sue pottery]] - Total: 17 (M4, others: 13). Includes six bowls, five lids, two tall stemmed vessels, and one flat bottle. Older Sue pottery types (before the Oda IVA period, TK209 type) are excluded{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. * [[Haji pottery]] - Total: 3 (M). Includes one bowl and two jars. == Burial Individual ==
'''Genealogical chart based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}''' {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||01| 01={{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||!|}} {{familytree|border=0|01|~|y|~|02| 01=Ōama no Ōji
({{Supra|40}} {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu}})|02={{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||!}} {{familytree|border=0||||01| 01={{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The individual buried in the Miyajidake Kofun is unknown, but they are presumed to be a chief of the ancient Munakata clan (宗形氏/宗像氏) from the Munakata region. Specifically, one theory identifies the buried individual as '''{{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi}}''' (むなかたのきみとくぜん). Munakata Tokuyoshi is believed to have been the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子}} (654?–696). According to the genealogical records in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, in the second year of Emperor Tenmu (673), Prince Ōama (later {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu}}) married Amako no Iratsume, the daughter of Munakata Tokuyoshi, producing Prince Takechi. While details are sparse due to limited mentions in other texts, Prince Takechi played a central role as the commander-in-chief of Emperor Ōama's forces during the Jinshin War and was later appointed {{ill|Daijō-daijin|ja|太政大臣}} in 690 under Empress Jitō. Munakata Tokuyoshi is therefore thought to have been instrumental in advancing the Munakata clan's influence within the central government「Munakata Tokuyoshi」『Dictionary of Ancient Japanese Clans, Popular Edition』, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2010.. Prince Takechi died in 696, with records in the {{ill|Kuge Bunin|ja|Kugyō補任}} stating he was 42 or 43 years old, while the {{ill|Fusō Ryakki|ja|扶桑略記}} records his age as 43. This suggests he was born around 654, placing Amako no Iratsume's marriage prior to that「Munakata Taisha」『Place names of Fukuoka Prefecture』, Japanese Historical Place names Series 41, Heibonsha, 2004.. No burial goods identifying a specific individual have been excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun. However, considering its relationship with the nearby Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun and Miyajidake Cremation Tomb, a connection to the ancient Munakata clan is plausible{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == Miyajidake Cremation Tomb == The '''Miyajidake Cremation Tomb''' (みやじだけかそうぼ) is an ancient {{ill|Cremation tomb|ja|火葬墓}} believed to have been located near the {{ill|Miyajidake Kofun|ja|宮地嶽古墳}}. The tomb was discovered in [[1938]] (Shōwa 13) on the western slope of a hill (approx. 65 meters above sea level) east of the stone chamber’s entrance during reforestation work. A glass funerary urn was unearthed about one shaku (approx. 30 cm) beneath the surface{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The urn was placed inside a ceramic composite jar and contained a glass short-necked urn with a lid, which was encased in a bronze lidded pedestal jar{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Since the ceramics were from a later period, they are considered secondary burial items, and the original tomb's location and structure remain unknown{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The glass funerary urn is similar in design and manufacturing techniques to one found in the grave of {{ill|Fumi no Nemaro|ja|文祢麻呂}} in {{ill|Uda City|ja|宇陀市}}, Nara Prefecture, which was dated to {{ill|Keiun|ja|慶雲}} 4 (707). This suggests the Miyajidake Cremation Tomb was constructed in the early [[8th century]]{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Hypotheses regarding the buried individual include {{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘}}, the daughter of {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善}}, or Munakata Tōjo, who is mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}} as having been appointed governor of Munakata District in [[Wadō|ja|和銅]] 2 (709){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The excavated funerary urn was designation1 a National Treasure in [[1961]] (Shōwa 36). == Historic site == === National Treasures === * burial goods Excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Kyushu National Museum (formerly in the Tokyo National Museum). Designated as a National Treasure on September 18, [[1936]], under the National Treasure Preservation Act; reclassified as Important Cultural Property under the [[Historic site Protection Law]] in [[1950]]; designation1 as a National Treasure on March 29, [[1952]]{{National Heritage Database|201|841|Miyajidake Kofun burial goods}}. * Glass Ossuary Excavated from the Grounds of Miyajidake Shrine (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Tokyo National Museum. Designated as a National Treasure (former Category) on October 25, [[1939]], under the National Treasure Preservation Act; reclassified as Important Cultural Property under the Historic site Protection Law in 1950; designation1 as a National Treasure (new Category) on April 27, [[1961]]{{National Heritage Database|201|861|Glass Ossuary from Miyajidake Shrine}}. === Related Facilities === * [[Kyushu National Museum]] ([[Dazaifu City]], [[Fukuoka Prefecture]]) - Stores burial goods from the Miyajidake Kofun. * [[Tokyo National Museum]] ([[Taitō City]], [[Tokyo]]) - Stores burial goods from the Miyajidake Cremation Tomb. == notes == {{reflist}} == References == {{small|(References used in writing this article)}} * Site explanation board * Encyclopedias ** {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=Mori Teijirō|year=|chapter=Miyajidake Kofun|title=[[National History Dictionary (Shōwa Period)|国史大辞典]]|publisher=[[Yoshikawa Kōbunkan]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|Miyajidake Kofun (National History)|}}}} ** {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=Harada Michio|year=1989|chapter=Miyajidake Kofun|title=[[Japanese Kofun Dictionary]]|publisher=[[Tōkyōdō Publishing]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Miyajidake Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} ** {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=|year=2004|chapter=Miyajidake Kofun|title=Fukuoka Prefecture Place names|series=[[Japanese Historical Place names Series]] 41|publisher=[[Heibonsha]]|isbn=4582490417|ref={{Harvid|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}}} * Others ** {{Cite journal|language=ja|author=Ikenoue Hiroshi, Hanada Katsuhiro|title=Reexamination of the Miyajidake Kofun in Chikushi|date=1999-12|publisher=Japan Archaeological Society|journal=Archaeological Journal|volume=85|number=1|pages=19-56|url=|naid=|doi=|ref={{Harvid|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}}} ** {{Cite journal|language=ja|author=Kojima Atsushi|title={{PDFlink|[https://www.munakata-archives.asia/Dat/bunken/0000000047_01.pdf "Munakata-no-Kimi as Viewed from the End of Keyhole-shaped Tumuli"]}}|date=2018|publisher=Munakata-Okinoshima and Associated Heritage Sites World Heritage Promotion Council|journal=Okinoshima Studies|volume=|number=4|pages=19-40|url=|naid=|doi=|ref={{Harvid|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}}} - Link from "Munakata Archives," Munakata-Okinoshima and Associated Heritage Sites Preservation and Utilization Council. == Related Literature == {{small|(Related literature not used in writing this article)}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|editor=|author=Shimada Torajirō|year=1939|chapter=Regarding the Fudō Cave of the Miyajidake Kofun|title=[https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/84360 Historic sites, Scenic Spots, and Natural Monuments Survey Report]|volume=No. 13, Historic sites Section|publisher=Fukuoka Prefecture|isbn=|ref=}} - {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 宮地嶽古墳 |画像 = [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, sendou.jpg|280px]]
石室内部 |別名 = 丸塚古墳/宮地嶽大塚 |所属 = [[津屋崎古墳群]] |所在地 = [[福岡県]][[福津市]]宮司元町1241（字大塚）（[[宮地嶽神社]]境内） |緯度度 = 33|緯度分 = 46|緯度秒 = 51.10 |経度度 = 130|経度分 = 29|経度秒 = 19.15 |ISO = JP-40 |形状 = [[円墳]] |規模 = 直径35m |埋葬施設 = [[横口式石槨]]系[[横穴式石室]] |出土品 = 金銅装頭椎大刀・金銅製馬具・金銅製冠・ガラス板・銅器など副葬品多数 |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]中葉 |被葬者 = （一説）[[宗形徳善|胸肩君徳善]] |陵墓 = |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「[[津屋崎古墳群]]」に包含 |有形文化財 = 出土品（[[国宝]]） |特記事項 = 石室は全国第2位の規模 |地図 = Japan Fukuoka |アイコン = 円墳 |ラベル = 宮地嶽古墳 |ラベル位置 = right }} '''宮地嶽古墳'''（みやじだけこふん）は、[[福岡県]][[福津市]]宮司元町にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。[[津屋崎古墳群]]（国の[[史跡]]）を構成する古墳の1つ。出土品は[[国宝]]に指定されている。 全国第2位の規模の巨大石室を有し、豪華な副葬品が多数出土したことで知られる。本項では、'''[[#宮地嶽火葬墓|宮地嶽火葬墓]]'''（出土品は国宝に指定）についても解説する。 == 概要 == [[File:Fudo Shrine (No.3 of Okunomiya 8 Shrines) in Miyajidake Shrine.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|不動神社（[[宮地嶽神社]]奥宮）}}{{small|石室開口部前に拝殿が建てられている。}}]] 福岡県北部、宮地岳（標高180.7メートル）山腹の南斜面上（標高約55メートル）に築造された大型円墳である{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。付近には古代の宮地嶽火葬墓の存在が推定されるほか、かつて斜面下には小古墳群が分布し、禊池を挟んだ丘陵上には宮司井手ノ上古墳が所在する{{Sfn|宮地嶽古墳（平凡社）|2004}}。現在は[[宮地嶽神社]]奥宮の不動神社として祀られる。[[江戸時代]]中期に石室が開口し、[[昭和]]期に副葬品が複数回出土しているほか、[[1937年|1937]]・[[1996年]]（昭和12・[[平成]]8年）に石室実測調査が実施されている（発掘調査は未実施）。 墳丘周囲は改変されているが、元は直径35メートル程度の円形と推定復元される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]系の[[横穴式石室]]で、東方向に開口する。石室全長23メートルを測る長大な石室であり、全国第2位の規模になるとして注目される。石室内の発掘調査は行われていないが、付近では長さ3メートル弱の長大な金銅装頭椎大刀を始めとして金銅製冠・金銅製馬具・ガラス板・銅器・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]などの、当初は石室内に納められた副葬品と見られる品が出土している。質・量とも優れており、特に唐草文の馬具や冠などには豊かな国際色が認められる点で注目される。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]中葉{{Sfn|小嶋篤|2018}}（または7世紀前半-中葉「津屋崎古墳群の評価 > 宮地嶽古墳」『津屋崎古墳群III』福津市教育委員会、2013年。/7世紀前半{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}、TK217型式期）頃と推定される。宗像地域の古代氏族である胸肩君（[[宗像氏]]）一族の首長墓とする説が有力視され、具体的な被葬者としては[[宗形徳善|胸肩君徳善]]とする説が挙げられる。巨大な横穴式石室、豪華な副葬品の点で、日本を代表する古墳の1つである。 古墳域は[[2005年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定され、出土品は[[1952年]]（昭和27年）に[[国宝]]に指定されている。現在では年3回の大祭時を除いて石室内部への立ち入りは制限されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[寛保]]元年（[[1741年]]）、大雨の際の土砂崩れで石室開口（[[天保]]年間（[[1830年|1830]]-[[1844年]]）編纂の『[[筑前国続風土記|筑前国続風土記拾遺]]』）{{Sfn|宮地嶽古墳（平凡社）|2004}}。 * [[延享]]4年（[[1747年]]）、石室奥に不動尊を奉斎（『筑前国続風土記拾遺』）{{Sfn|宮地嶽古墳（平凡社）|2004}}。 * [[1930年]]（[[昭和]]5年）の遷宮に合わせて、古墳周辺に付帯施設の建設{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 * [[1934年]]（昭和9年）、社務所建設の際に馬具・刀剣類の出土{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 ** [[1936年]]（昭和11年）9月18日、[[国宝保存法]]に基づき馬具等が国宝（旧国宝）に指定。 * [[1937年]]（昭和12年）、石室実測調査（鏡山猛）{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 * [[1938年]]（昭和13年）、古墳東側で植樹作業の際にガラス蔵骨器の出土{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 ** [[1939年]]（昭和14年）10月25日、国宝保存法に基づき蔵骨器が国宝（旧国宝）に指定。 * [[1951年]]（昭和26年）、羨門前から冠片等の出土{{Sfn|宮地嶽古墳（平凡社）|2004}}。 ** [[1952年]]（昭和27年）3月29日、出土品が[[国宝]]（新国宝）に指定。 ** [[1961年]]（昭和36年）4月27日、蔵骨器が国宝（新国宝）に指定。 * [[1996年]]（平成8年）、石室再実測調査（池ノ上宏ら、[[1999年]]に報告）{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 ** [[2005年]]（平成17年）3月2日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[津屋崎古墳群]]」のうち）{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|3422|津屋崎古墳群}}。 == 墳丘 == [[File:Miyajidake-Tumulus 20161014.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|墳丘}}{{small|現在は墳丘周囲に列石が巡る。}}]] 墳丘は緩斜面の尾根を切断し、地山の整形を行ったうえで構築されている{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。現在の墳丘は、南北27メートル・東西34メートルの楕円形を呈するが、元は直径35メートル程度の円形と推定復元される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。墳丘上には、厚さ2メートル程度の2次盛土が認められているが、これは1934年（昭和9年）以前の石室内の掘り下げ時の排土とされる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 墳丘周囲には、幅1メートル・高さ1.4メートル程度の石による列石が巡らされ、羨門両側では3段に積む{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。列石は1934年（昭和9年）以前に設置されたもので、墳丘周囲を削平しており、元はそれ以上に墳丘が広がっていたと見られる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 == 埋葬施設 == [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-1.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|石室俯瞰図}}]] [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石室展開図}}]] 埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]系[[横穴式石室]]で、東方向に開口する。羨道・玄室のうち、玄室の奥側は一回り狭まって奥室・前室に区分され、畿内の横口式石槨同様の複室構造を呈する。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 * 石室全長：約23.1メートル（現状23.5-24メートル） * 石槨（奥室）：長さ3.5メートル、幅約1.75メートル * 玄室（前室）：長さ11.7メートル、幅2.5-2.8メートル、高さ2.2-3.1メートル ** 左龕（南龕）：長さ1.9メートル、奥行0.7メートル、高さ1.5メートル ** 右龕（北龕）：長さ1.9メートル、奥行0.7メートル、高さ1.3メートル 石室の石材は恋ノ浦海岸の礫岩とされる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。巨石が使用されており、海岸部から中腹まで引き上げる際に多大な労力が必要となったことが示唆される{{Sfn|小嶋篤|2018}}。石室は[[丸山古墳 (橿原市)|五条野丸山古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[橿原市]]）の全長28.4メートルに次ぐ全国第2位の規模になる。 石槨（奥から1石目）では、約3メートルの一枚石3個を組む。玄室（奥から2-4石目）は、両側壁に高さ3.1-4.5メートルの一枚石を立て並べる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。特に2石目の左右には石材を刳って龕が形成されており、その石材は石室内で最も大きな石で、厚さ1.7メートル以上を測る{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。江戸時代の記録に基づけば、龕は当初から存在したと見られる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。羨道（奥から5-7石目）は、2-3段積みとする{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。羨門付近には0.3-0.4メートルの塊石が不規則に積み上げられるが、これは2次的な石積みとされる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。床面は、現在ではコンクリート打ちのため詳らかとしないが、元は全体に玉石による敷石をした上に、床石を配したと推測される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。天井石は、石槨では厚さ0.5メートル、2石目（龕）上では厚さ1メートル、4石目上では厚さ1.65メートルを測る{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 宮地嶽古墳と同様の石室構造を持つ古墳としては、[[手光波切不動古墳]]（福津市手光）が知られる。かつては宮地嶽古墳→手光波切不動古墳の築造順と見られていたが{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}、[[2010年|2010]]-[[2011年]]度（平成22-23年度）の手光波切不動古墳の調査等を踏まえて、近年では手光波切不動古墳→宮地嶽古墳の築造順と推測される{{Sfn|小嶋篤|2018}}。 {{small|奥の1石目が石槨部分。手前の2石目（玄室部分）の側壁には龕が形成される。}} Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-1.jpg|玄室（奥壁方向） Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-2.jpg|玄室（開口部方向） Miyajidake Kofun, entrance.jpg|開口部付近（奥壁方向） == 出土品 == [[File:HARNESS MIYAJIDAKE.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{center|金銅製壺鐙（[[国宝]]）}}]] 昭和期に古墳付近から出土した副葬品は次の通り{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。宮地嶽神社所蔵品（東京国立博物館のち九州国立博物館寄託品、国宝指定）にはMを付して掲載する。 * 大刀 ** 金銅装頭椎大刀（大型） 1（M） - 推定全長2.4-2.8メートル。柄頭・鐔・鞘金具・刀身が遺存。 ** 金銅装頭椎大刀 1（M） - 推定全長0.90メートル。柄頭・鎺金具・鞘尻金具・刀身が遺存。 * 馬具 ** 金銅製鞍（前輪、後輪、磯金具） 1個体（M） - 前輪・後輪の覆輪はほぼ完存、それ以外の金具のほとんどは欠失。 ** 金銅製壺鐙 2（M） ** 金銅製鏡板付轡 2（M） ** 金銅製杏葉 2（M） ** 鞍（唐草文金具） 1（M） ** 鉸具（鉄製） 1（M） ** 鉸具（金銅製鞍金具など） 7（M） * ガラス板 3個体（M） - ガラス玉の原材料か。 * ガラス板（破片） 27（M19、他8+） * 砥石 1（M） * 金銅製透彫冠 1（M） * ガラス玉（大・中） 265（M256、他6） - 鉛ガラス製、緑色半透明。 * 金環 3（M1、他2） * 銅鈴 3（M2、他1） * 銅釘 4（M） * 飾金具 2（M） * 金具（その他） 2（M） * 銅鎖 1個体（18環）（M） * 銅器 2（M） - 蓋付銅鋺1、承盤1。 * 銅製刀子（鞘金具） 1個体（M） * [[須恵器]] 17（M4、他13） - 坏身6、坏蓋5、高坏2、平瓶1など。小田IVA期（TK209型式期）以前の須恵器は含まない{{Sfn|小嶋篤|2018}}。 * [[土師器]] 3（M） - 坏1、壺2。 == 被葬者 ==
'''『[[日本書紀]]』に基づく関係系図''' {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||01| 01=[[宗形徳善|胸肩君徳善]]}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||!|}} {{familytree|border=0|01|~|y|~|02| 01=大海人皇子
（{{Supra|40}} [[天武天皇]]）|02=[[尼子娘]]}} {{familytree|border=0|||||!}} {{familytree|border=0||||01| 01=[[高市皇子]]}} {{familytree/end}}
宮地嶽古墳の被葬者は明らかでないが、宗像地域の古代氏族である[[宗像氏|胸肩君]]（宗形氏/宗像氏）の首長と推定され、具体的な被葬者としては'''[[宗形徳善|胸肩君徳善]]'''（むなかたのきみとくぜん）とする説が挙げられる。胸肩君徳善は、[[高市皇子]]（[[654年|654]]?-[[696年]]）の外祖父とされる人物である。 『[[日本書紀]]』[[天武天皇]]2年（[[673年]]）2月癸未（27日）条の皇統譜によれば、大海人皇子（第40代[[天武天皇]]）は胸形君徳善の娘の[[尼子娘]]と婚姻関係を持ち、高市皇子をもうけている。他の文献に記述が見られないため詳らかでないが、高市皇子は[[壬申の乱]]で大海人皇子軍の統帥となり、[[持統天皇]]4年（[[690年]]）には[[太政大臣]]に任じられていることから、外祖父の胸形君徳善は宗形氏の中央進出のきっかけになった人物と想定される「胸形君徳善」 『日本古代氏族人名辞典 普及版』吉川弘文館、2010年。。高市皇子は持統天皇10年（[[696年]]）に死去するが、その際の年齢を『[[公卿補任]]』では42歳または43歳、『[[扶桑略記]]』では43歳としており、[[白雉]]5年（[[654年]]）頃の生まれと見られることから、尼子娘の婚姻もそれ以前と推測される「宗像大社」 『福岡県の地名』日本歴史地名大系41、平凡社、2004年。。 宮地嶽古墳からは具体的な人物名を示唆する遺物は出土していないが、手光波切不動古墳・宮地嶽火葬墓の存在を考え合わせて、古代宗形氏との関連性が推測される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 == 宮地嶽火葬墓 == '''宮地嶽火葬墓'''（みやじだけかそうぼ）は、宮地嶽古墳の付近にあったと見られる[[古代]][[火葬墓]]。 宮地嶽古墳の石室開口部から東方向の丘陵西斜面上（標高約65メートル）において、[[1938年]]（昭和13年）に植樹作業中に表面下約1尺からガラス製蔵骨器が出土したことで発見された{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。蔵骨器は陶質の合せ甕（鉢）の中に入っており、銅製有蓋高台壺の中にガラス製有蓋短頸壺を納める{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。土器は後世のものであるため、再埋納品とされ、本来の墓の所在・構造は明らかでない{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 ガラス製蔵骨器は、[[書根麻呂|文祢麻呂]]墓（[[奈良県]][[宇陀市]]）のものと形態・製作技法が類似するが、同墓では[[慶雲]]4年（[[707年]]）銘の墓誌が出土していることから、宮地嶽火葬墓も同様に[[8世紀]]初頭頃の築造と推定される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。被葬者としては、胸肩君徳善の娘の[[尼子娘]]とする説や、『[[続日本紀]]』[[和銅]]2年（[[709年]]）に宗像郡大領に任じられたと見える宗形等抒とする説がある{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 出土蔵骨器は[[1961年]]（昭和36年）に国宝に指定されている。 == 文化財 == === 国宝 === * 宮地嶽古墳出土品（考古資料） *: 明細は後出。所有者は宮地嶽古墳、九州国立博物館保管（以前は東京国立博物館保管）。1936年（昭和11年）9月18日に[[国宝保存法]]に基づき国宝（旧国宝）に指定、1950年（昭和25年）の[[文化財保護法]]施行により国の重要文化財に指定、1952年（昭和27年）3月29日に国宝（新国宝）に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|841|宮地嶽古墳出土品}}。 * 筑前国宮地嶽神社境内出土骨蔵器（考古資料） *: 明細は後出。所有者は宮地嶽古墳、東京国立博物館保管。1939年（昭和14年）10月25日に国宝保存法に基づき国宝（旧国宝）に指定、1950年（昭和25年）の文化財保護法施行により国の重要文化財に指定、1961年（昭和36年）4月27日に国宝（新国宝）に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|861|筑前国宮地嶽神社境内出土骨蔵器}}。 {{hidden begin |title = 国宝「宮地嶽古墳出土品」・「筑前国宮地嶽神社境内出土骨蔵器」の明細 |border = #aaa solid 1px |titlestyle = text-align: center; background:lightgrey; }} ; 宮地嶽古墳出土品 * 金銅鞍金具残欠 1背 - 前後両橋 覆輪、海磯金具鞖等。 * 金銅壺鐙 1双 * 金銅鏡板付轡 1箇分 * 金銅杏葉残欠 2枚分 * 銅鎖 1連 * 金銅装頭椎大刀（大形）残欠 1口分 - 柄頭、鐔、刀身断片、鞘金具等。 * 金銅装頭椎大刀残欠 1口分 - 柄頭、鎺、刀身断片等。 * 金銅透彫冠残欠 一括 * 金環 1箇 * 緑瑠璃丸玉 1連 * 緑瑠璃丸玉 一括 * 蓋付銅鋺 1口 * 銅盤残欠 1枚分 * 土師器盌 1口 * 長方形緑瑠璃板残欠 3枚分 * 緑瑠璃板断片 一括 * （附指定）各種金具等残片 一括 ; 筑前国宮地嶽神社境内出土骨蔵器 * 瑠璃壺 1合 * 銅壺 1合 * （附指定）陶質鉢残闕 2口分 {{hidden end}} == 関連施設 == * [[九州国立博物館]]（[[福岡県]][[太宰府市]]） - 宮地嶽古墳の出土品を保管。 * [[東京国立博物館]]（[[東京都]][[台東区]]） - 宮地獄火葬墓の出土品を保管。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板 * 事典類 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=森貞次郎|year=|chapter=宮地嶽古墳|title=[[国史大辞典 (昭和時代)|国史大辞典]]|publisher=[[吉川弘文館]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|宮地嶽古墳（国史）}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=原田道雄|year=1989|chapter=宮地嶽古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|宮地嶽古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2004|chapter=宮地嶽古墳|title=福岡県の地名|series=[[日本歴史地名大系]]41|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490417|ref={{Harvid|宮地嶽古墳（平凡社）|2004}}}} * その他 ** {{Cite journal|和書|author=池ノ上宏・花田勝広|title=筑紫・宮地嶽古墳の再検討|date=1999-12|publisher=日本考古学会|journal=考古学雑誌|volume=85|number=1|pages=19-56|url=|naid=|doi=|ref={{Harvid|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}}} ** {{Cite journal|和書|author=小嶋篤|title={{PDFlink|[https://www.munakata-archives.asia/Dat/bunken/0000000047_01.pdf 「前方後円墳の終焉」から見た胸肩君]}}|date=2018|publisher=宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群世界遺産推進会議|journal=沖ノ島研究|volume=|number=4|pages=19-40|url=|naid=|doi=|ref={{Harvid|小嶋篤|2018}}}} - リンクは世界遺産「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群保存活用協議会「MUNAKATA ARCHIVES」。 == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=島田寅次郎|year=1939|chapter=石器と土器・古墳と副葬品 > 宮地嶽古墳の不動窟につきて|title=[https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/84360 史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告書]|volume=第13輯 史蹟之部|publisher=福岡県|isbn=|ref=}} - リンクは奈良文化財研究所「全国遺跡報告総覧」。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1968|chapter=|title=國寶宮地嶽古墳出土品修理報告書|publisher=宮地嶽神社|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=[[小田富士雄]]|year=1982|chapter=宮地嶽古墳|title=探訪日本の古墳|volume=西日本編|publisher=有斐閣|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2022|chapter=|title=よみがえる黄金の宝 国宝宮地嶽古墳出土宝物の世界（大野城市市制50周年記念特別展）|publisher=大野城心のふるさと館|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[宮地嶽神社]] * [[津屋崎古墳群]] ** [[手光波切不動古墳]] * [[宗像大社]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Miyajidake Kofun}} * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/841 宮地嶽古墳出土品]、[https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/861 筑前国宮地嶽神社境内出土骨蔵器] - 国指定文化財等データベース（[[文化庁]]） * [https://www.fukuoka-bunkazai.jp/frmDetail.aspx?db=1&id=45 宮地嶽古墳出土品] - 福岡県教育庁教育総務部文化財保護課「福岡県の文化財」 {{リダイレクトの所属カテゴリ |redirect1=宮地嶽火葬墓 |1-1=日本の墓地 |1-2=福岡県の考古遺跡 |1-3=福津市の歴史 |1-4=奈良時代の遺跡 |1-5=宗像氏 }} {{DEFAULTSORT:みやしたけこふん}} [[Category:福岡県の古墳]] [[Category:福津市の歴史]] [[Category:円墳]] [[Category:日本の国宝 (考古・歴史資料)]] [[Category:福岡県の国宝]] [[Category:福岡県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:宗像氏|墓みやしたけこふん]]

{{日本の古墳 |名称 = 宮地嶽古墳 |画像 = [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, sendou.jpg|280px]]
石室内部 |別名 = 丸塚古墳/宮地嶽大塚 |所属 = [[津屋崎古墳群]] |所在地 = [[福岡県]][[福津市]]宮司元町1241（字大塚）（[[宮地嶽神社]]境内） |緯度度 = 33|緯度分 = 46|緯度秒 = 51.10 |経度度 = 130|経度分 = 29|経度秒 = 19.15 |ISO = JP-40 |形状 = [[円墳]] |規模 = 直径35m |埋葬施設 = [[横口式石槨]]系[[横穴式石室]] |出土品 = 金銅装頭椎大刀・金銅製馬具・金銅製冠・ガラス板・銅器など副葬品多数 |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]中葉 |被葬者 = （一説）[[宗形徳善|胸肩君徳善]] |陵墓 = |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「[[津屋崎古墳群]]」に包含 |有形文化財 = 出土品（[[国宝]]） |特記事項 = 石室は全国第2位の規模 |地図 = Japan Fukuoka |アイコン = 円墳 |ラベル = 宮地嶽古墳 |ラベル位置 = right }} '''宮地嶽古墳'''（みやじだけこふん）は、[[福岡県]][[福津市]]宮司元町にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。[[津屋崎古墳群]]（国の[[史跡]]）を構成する古墳の1つ。出土品は[[国宝]]に指定されている。 全国第2位の規模の巨大石室を有し、豪華な副葬品が多数出土したことで知られる。本項では、'''[[#宮地嶽火葬墓|宮地嶽火葬墓]]'''（出土品は国宝に指定）についても解説する。 == 概要 == [[File:Fudo Shrine (No.3 of Okunomiya 8 Shrines) in Miyajidake Shrine.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|不動神社（[[宮地嶽神社]]奥宮）}}{{small|石室開口部前に拝殿が建てられている。}}]] 福岡県北部、宮地岳（標高180.7メートル）山腹の南斜面上（標高約55メートル）に築造された大型円墳である{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。付近には古代の宮地嶽火葬墓の存在が推定されるほか、かつて斜面下には小古墳群が分布し、禊池を挟んだ丘陵上には宮司井手ノ上古墳が所在する{{Sfn|宮地嶽古墳（平凡社）|2004}}。現在は[[宮地嶽神社]]奥宮の不動神社として祀られる。[[江戸時代]]中期に石室が開口し、[[昭和]]期に副葬品が複数回出土しているほか、[[1937年|1937]]・[[1996年]]（昭和12・[[平成]]8年）に石室実測調査が実施されている（発掘調査は未実施）。 墳丘周囲は改変されているが、元は直径35メートル程度の円形と推定復元される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]系の[[横穴式石室]]で、東方向に開口する。石室全長23メートルを測る長大な石室であり、全国第2位の規模になるとして注目される。石室内の発掘調査は行われていないが、付近では長さ3メートル弱の長大な金銅装頭椎大刀を始めとして金銅製冠・金銅製馬具・ガラス板・銅器・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]などの、当初は石室内に納められた副葬品と見られる品が出土している。質・量とも優れており、特に唐草文の馬具や冠などには豊かな国際色が認められる点で注目される。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]中葉{{Sfn|小嶋篤|2018}}（または7世紀前半-中葉「津屋崎古墳群の評価 > 宮地嶽古墳」『津屋崎古墳群III』福津市教育委員会、2013年。/7世紀前半{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}、TK217型式期）頃と推定される。宗像地域の古代氏族である胸肩君（[[宗像氏]]）一族の首長墓とする説が有力視され、具体的な被葬者としては[[宗形徳善|胸肩君徳善]]とする説が挙げられる。巨大な横穴式石室、豪華な副葬品の点で、日本を代表する古墳の1つである。 古墳域は[[2005年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定され、出土品は[[1952年]]（昭和27年）に[[国宝]]に指定されている。現在では年3回の大祭時を除いて石室内部への立ち入りは制限されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[寛保]]元年（[[1741年]]）、大雨の際の土砂崩れで石室開口（[[天保]]年間（[[1830年|1830]]-[[1844年]]）編纂の『[[筑前国続風土記|筑前国続風土記拾遺]]』）{{Sfn|宮地嶽古墳（平凡社）|2004}}。 * [[延享]]4年（[[1747年]]）、石室奥に不動尊を奉斎（『筑前国続風土記拾遺』）{{Sfn|宮地嶽古墳（平凡社）|2004}}。 * [[1930年]]（[[昭和]]5年）の遷宮に合わせて、古墳周辺に付帯施設の建設{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 * [[1934年]]（昭和9年）、社務所建設の際に馬具・刀剣類の出土{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 ** [[1936年]]（昭和11年）9月18日、[[国宝保存法]]に基づき馬具等が国宝（旧国宝）に指定。 * [[1937年]]（昭和12年）、石室実測調査（鏡山猛）{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 * [[1938年]]（昭和13年）、古墳東側で植樹作業の際にガラス蔵骨器の出土{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 ** [[1939年]]（昭和14年）10月25日、国宝保存法に基づき蔵骨器が国宝（旧国宝）に指定。 * [[1951年]]（昭和26年）、羨門前から冠片等の出土{{Sfn|宮地嶽古墳（平凡社）|2004}}。 ** [[1952年]]（昭和27年）3月29日、出土品が[[国宝]]（新国宝）に指定。 ** [[1961年]]（昭和36年）4月27日、蔵骨器が国宝（新国宝）に指定。 * [[1996年]]（平成8年）、石室再実測調査（池ノ上宏ら、[[1999年]]に報告）{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 ** [[2005年]]（平成17年）3月2日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[津屋崎古墳群]]」のうち）{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|3422|津屋崎古墳群}}。 == 墳丘 == [[File:Miyajidake-Tumulus 20161014.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|墳丘}}{{small|現在は墳丘周囲に列石が巡る。}}]] 墳丘は緩斜面の尾根を切断し、地山の整形を行ったうえで構築されている{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。現在の墳丘は、南北27メートル・東西34メートルの楕円形を呈するが、元は直径35メートル程度の円形と推定復元される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。墳丘上には、厚さ2メートル程度の2次盛土が認められているが、これは1934年（昭和9年）以前の石室内の掘り下げ時の排土とされる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 墳丘周囲には、幅1メートル・高さ1.4メートル程度の石による列石が巡らされ、羨門両側では3段に積む{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。列石は1934年（昭和9年）以前に設置されたもので、墳丘周囲を削平しており、元はそれ以上に墳丘が広がっていたと見られる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 == 埋葬施設 == [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-1.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|石室俯瞰図}}]] [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石室展開図}}]] 埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]系[[横穴式石室]]で、東方向に開口する。羨道・玄室のうち、玄室の奥側は一回り狭まって奥室・前室に区分され、畿内の横口式石槨同様の複室構造を呈する。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 * 石室全長：約23.1メートル（現状23.5-24メートル） * 石槨（奥室）：長さ3.5メートル、幅約1.75メートル * 玄室（前室）：長さ11.7メートル、幅2.5-2.8メートル、高さ2.2-3.1メートル ** 左龕（南龕）：長さ1.9メートル、奥行0.7メートル、高さ1.5メートル ** 右龕（北龕）：長さ1.9メートル、奥行0.7メートル、高さ1.3メートル 石室の石材は恋ノ浦海岸の礫岩とされる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。巨石が使用されており、海岸部から中腹まで引き上げる際に多大な労力が必要となったことが示唆される{{Sfn|小嶋篤|2018}}。石室は[[丸山古墳 (橿原市)|五条野丸山古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[橿原市]]）の全長28.4メートルに次ぐ全国第2位の規模になる。 石槨（奥から1石目）では、約3メートルの一枚石3個を組む。玄室（奥から2-4石目）は、両側壁に高さ3.1-4.5メートルの一枚石を立て並べる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。特に2石目の左右には石材を刳って龕が形成されており、その石材は石室内で最も大きな石で、厚さ1.7メートル以上を測る{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。江戸時代の記録に基づけば、龕は当初から存在したと見られる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。羨道（奥から5-7石目）は、2-3段積みとする{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。羨門付近には0.3-0.4メートルの塊石が不規則に積み上げられるが、これは2次的な石積みとされる{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。床面は、現在ではコンクリート打ちのため詳らかとしないが、元は全体に玉石による敷石をした上に、床石を配したと推測される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。天井石は、石槨では厚さ0.5メートル、2石目（龕）上では厚さ1メートル、4石目上では厚さ1.65メートルを測る{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 宮地嶽古墳と同様の石室構造を持つ古墳としては、[[手光波切不動古墳]]（福津市手光）が知られる。かつては宮地嶽古墳→手光波切不動古墳の築造順と見られていたが{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}、[[2010年|2010]]-[[2011年]]度（平成22-23年度）の手光波切不動古墳の調査等を踏まえて、近年では手光波切不動古墳→宮地嶽古墳の築造順と推測される{{Sfn|小嶋篤|2018}}。 '''『[[日本書紀]]』に基づく関係系図''' {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||01| 01=[[宗形徳善|胸肩君徳善]]}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||!|}} {{familytree|border=0|01|~|y|~|02| 01=大海人皇子
（{{Supra|40}} [[天武天皇]]）|02=[[尼子娘]]}} {{familytree|border=0|||||!}} {{familytree|border=0||||01| 01=[[高市皇子]]}} {{familytree/end}}
宮地嶽古墳の被葬者は明らかでないが、宗像地域の古代氏族である[[宗像氏|胸肩君]]（宗形氏/宗像氏）の首長と推定され、具体的な被葬者としては'''[[宗形徳善|胸肩君徳善]]'''（むなかたのきみとくぜん）とする説が挙げられる。胸肩君徳善は、[[高市皇子]]（[[654年|654]]?-[[696年]]）の外祖父とされる人物である。 『[[日本書紀]]』[[天武天皇]]2年（[[673年]]）2月癸未（27日）条の皇統譜によれば、大海人皇子（第40代[[天武天皇]]）は胸形君徳善の娘の[[尼子娘]]と婚姻関係を持ち、高市皇子をもうけている。他の文献に記述が見られないため詳らかでないが、高市皇子は[[壬申の乱]]で大海人皇子軍の統帥となり、[[持統天皇]]4年（[[690年]]）には[[太政大臣]]に任じられていることから、外祖父の胸形君徳善は宗形氏の中央進出のきっかけになった人物と想定される「胸形君徳善」 『日本古代氏族人名辞典 普及版』吉川弘文館、2010年。。高市皇子は持統天皇10年（[[696年]]）に死去するが、その際の年齢を『[[公卿補任]]』では42歳または43歳、『[[扶桑略記]]』では43歳としており、[[白雉]]5年（[[654年]]）頃の生まれと見られることから、尼子娘の婚姻もそれ以前と推測される「宗像大社」 『福岡県の地名』日本歴史地名大系41、平凡社、2004年。。 宮地嶽古墳からは具体的な人物名を示唆する遺物は出土していないが、手光波切不動古墳・宮地嶽火葬墓の存在を考え合わせて、古代宗形氏との関連性が推測される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 == 宮地嶽火葬墓 == '''宮地嶽火葬墓'''（みやじだけかそうぼ）は、宮地嶽古墳の付近にあったと見られる[[古代]][[火葬墓]]。 宮地嶽古墳の石室開口部から東方向の丘陵西斜面上（標高約65メートル）において、[[1938年]]（昭和13年）に植樹作業中に表面下約1尺からガラス製蔵骨器が出土したことで発見された{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。蔵骨器は陶質の合せ甕（鉢）の中に入っており、銅製有蓋高台壺の中にガラス製有蓋短頸壺を納める{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。土器は後世のものであるため、再埋納品とされ、本来の墓の所在・構造は明らかでない{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 ガラス製蔵骨器は、[[書根麻呂|文祢麻呂]]墓（[[奈良県]][[宇陀市]]）のものと形態・製作技法が類似するが、同墓では[[慶雲]]4年（[[707年]]）銘の墓誌が出土していることから、宮地嶽火葬墓も同様に[[8世紀]]初頭頃の築造と推定される{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。被葬者としては、胸肩君徳善の娘の[[尼子娘]]とする説や、『[[続日本紀]]』[[和銅]]2年（[[709年]]）に宗像郡大領に任じられたと見える宗形等抒とする説がある{{Sfn|池ノ上宏・花田勝広|1999}}。 出土蔵骨器は[[1961年]]（昭和36年）に国宝に指定されている。 == 文化財 == === 国宝 === * 宮地嶽古墳出土品（考古資料） *: 明細は後出。所有者は宮地嶽古墳、九州国立博物館保管（以前は東京国立博物館保管）。1936年（昭和11年）9月18日に[[国宝保存法]]に基づき国宝（旧国宝）に指定、1950年（昭和25年）の[[文化財保護法]]施行により国の重要文化財に指定、1952年（昭和27年）3月29日に国宝（新国宝）に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|841|宮地嶽古墳出土品}}。 * 筑前国宮地嶽神社境内出土骨蔵器（考古資料） *: 明細は後出。所有者は宮地嶽古墳、東京国立博物館保管。1939年（昭和14年）10月25日に国宝保存法に基づき国宝（旧国宝）に指定、1950年（昭和25年）の文化財保護法施行により国の重要文化財に指定、1961年（昭和36年）4月27日に国宝（新国宝）に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|861|筑前国宮地嶽神社境内出土骨蔵器}}。 {{hidden begin |title = 国宝「宮地嶽古墳出土品」・「筑前国宮地嶽神社境内出土骨蔵器」の明細 |border = #aaa solid 1px |titlestyle = text-align: center; background:lightgrey; }} ; 宮地嶽古墳出土品 * 金銅鞍金具残欠 1背 - It is a {{ill|round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} and one of the Kofuns comprising the {{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群}}, designation1 as a National Historic site. The burial items excavated from the mound are classified as a National Treasure. This kofun is known for having the second-largest stone chamber in Japan and for the discovery of numerous luxurious burial items. This article also includes information on the [[Miyajidake Kofun#Miyajidake Cremation Tomb|Miyajidake Cremation Tomb]], whose burial items are also designation1 as National Treasures. == Overview == [[File:Fudo Shrine (No.3 of Okunomiya 8 Shrines) in Miyajidake Shrine.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fudō Shrine (Okunomiya of Miyajidake Shrine)}}{{small|The hall of worship is built in front of the stone chamber opening.}}]] Miyajidake Kofun is a large circular Kofun constructed on the southern slope (approximately 55 meters above sea level) of Mount Miyajidake (elevation 180.7 meters) in northern Fukuoka Prefecture{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Nearby, ancient cremation graves associated with Miyajidake are believed to exist, and the surrounding area once featured small Kofuns. On a hill across the Misogi Pond, the {{ill|Miyaji Idenoue Kofun|ja|宮司井手ノ上古墳}} is located{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Currently, the site is worshipped as Fudō Shrine, an Okunomiya (inner shrine) of Miyajidake Shrine. The stone chamber was opened in the mid-Edo period, and burial items were excavated multiple times during the Shōwa era. Measured surveys of the chamber were conducted in 1937 and 1996 (Shōwa 12 and Heisei 8), but no full excavation has been carried out. While the Kofun has been modified over time, it is estimated to have originally been a circular mound approximately 35 meters in diameter{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}-type horizontal stone chamber, which opens to the east. The chamber, with a total length of 23 meters, is the second-largest of its kind in Japan. Though no excavations have been conducted inside the chamber, burial items believed to have originally been stored there have been discovered nearby, including a gilded bronze-headed tachi sword nearly 3 meters long, a gilded bronze crown, gilded bronze horse gear, glass plates, bronze ware, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}. These burial goods are notable for their exceptional quality and quantity, and the horse gear and crown, adorned with arabesque patterns, reflect rich international influences. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the mid-7th century, during the {{ill|final stage of the Kofun period|ja|古墳時代終末期}}{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}} (or in the early to mid-7th century"Evaluation of the Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster > Miyajidake Kofun," *Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster III*, Fukutsu City Board of Education, 2013. / early 7th century{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, TK217-style period). It is widely regarded as the tomb of a leader from the Munakata clan, an ancient clan in the Munakata region. The specific interred individual is often identified as {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善}}. The combination of the massive stone chamber and the luxurious burial items makes Miyajidake Kofun one of Japan's representative Kofuns. The burial site was designation1 a National Historic site in 2005 (Heisei 17), and its burial items were designation1 a National Treasure in 1952 (Shōwa 27). Access to the interior of the stone chamber is currently restricted except during the three annual grand festivals. == Archaeological History == * In the first year of the [[Kanpō]] era ([[1741]]), the stone chamber was exposed due to a landslide during heavy rain (as documented in the {{ill|Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel|ja|筑前国続風土記拾遺}} compiled during the [[Tenpō]] era ([[1830]]–[[1844]])){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In the 4th year of the [[Enkyō]] era ([[1747]]), the deity Fudō Myōō was enshrined at the back of the stone chamber (as documented in the 'Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel'){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In [[1930]] (the 5th year of the [[Shōwa]] era), ancillary facilities were constructed around the tumulus in conjunction with the shrine's relocation{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1934]] (Shōwa 9), equestrian gear and swords were excavated during the construction of the shrine Database|401|3422|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster}}. == Mound == [[File:Miyajidake-Kofun 20161014.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}{{small|Today, stone rows encircle the mound.}}]] The mound was built by cutting through the gentle slope of a ridge and reshaping the natural terrain{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The current mound has an elliptical type, measuring 27 meters north-south and 34 meters east-west, but it is estimated to have originally been a circular type with a diameter of about 35 meters{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A secondary layer of earth, approximately 2 meters thick, is observed on the mound, which is believed to be the soil excavated during the 1934 digging of the stone chamber{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Around the mound, rows of stones about 1 meter wide and 1.4 meters high encircle the structure, with three-tiered stacking near the dromos{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. These stone rows were installed before 1934 and are believed to have reduced the original size of the mound{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == burial == [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-1.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Bird's-eye view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Expanded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility is a {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber with a side entrance|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}} type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening towards the east. Among the passageway and main chamber, the rear section of the main chamber is slightly narrower, divided into a rear chamber and a front chamber, showcasing a multi-chamber structure similar to horizontal stone chambers in the Kinai region. The area of the stone chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}: * Total length of the stone chamber: Approx. 23.1 meters (current measurement: 23.5–24 meters) * Stone sarcophagus (rear chamber): Length 3.5 meters, width approx. 1.75 meters * Main chamber (front chamber): Length 11.7 meters, width 2.5–2.8 meters, height 2.2–3.1 meters ** Left niche (south niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.5 meters ** Right niche (north niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.3 meters The stone material for the chamber is said to be conglomerate rock from the Koi no Ura coast{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Large stones were used, suggesting significant labor was required to transport them from the coast to the mid-slope area{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. The stone chamber is the second largest nationwide after the {{ill|Maruyama Kofun (Kashihara)|ja|丸山古墳 (橿原市)}} (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture), with a total length of 28.4 meters. In the stone sarcophagus (first stone from the rear), three approximately 3-meter monolithic stones are assembled. The main chamber (second to fourth stones from the rear) features monolithic stones, 3.1–4.5 meters in height, standing side by side on both sidewalls{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Particularly on the second stone from the rear, niches have been carved into both sides of the stone, which is the largest stone in the chamber, measuring more than 1.7 meters in thickness{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Historical records from the Edo period indicate that these niches existed from the beginning{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The passageway (fifth to seventh stones from the rear) is constructed with two to three layers of stacked stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Near the entrance, stones 0.3–0.4 meters in size are irregularly piled, considered to be secondary stonework{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The floor, currently covered with concrete, was likely originally paved with pebbles and arranged with floor stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The ceiling stones measure 0.5 meters thick in the sarcophagus area, 1 meter above the second stone (niche area), and 1.65 meters above the fourth stone{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A similar stone chamber structure to the Miyajidake Kofun is known from the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳}} in Fukutsu City. Previously, the Miyajidake Kofun was thought to precede the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, but based on investigations from 2010–2011 (Heisei 22–23), it is now hypothesized that the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun predates the Miyajidake Kofun{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. Niches are formed on the sidewalls of the second stone in the main chamber.}} Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-1.jpg|Main chamber (towards the rear wall) Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-2.jpg|Main chamber (towards the entrance) Miyajidake Kofun, entrance.jpg|Entrance area (towards the rear wall) == burial goods == [[File:HARNESS MIYAJIDAKE.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Gilt Bronze Stirrup (National Treasure)}}]] The grave goods excavated near the tumulus during the Shōwa period are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Items owned by Miyajidake Shrine (formerly stored in the Tokyo National Museum, later deposited in the Kyushu National Museum, and designation1 as National Treasures) are marked with an "M." * Swords ** Large gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 2.4–2.8 meters. Parts including the pommel, guard, sheath fittings, and blade remain. ** Gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 0.90 meters. Parts including the pommel, habaki fitting, sheath tip fitting, and blade remain. * Horse gear ** Gilt bronze saddle fittings (M) - Front and rear bridges are mostly intact, but most other fittings are missing. ** Gilt bronze stirrups (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze bridles with decorative plates (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze pendants (pair) (M) ** Saddle with arabesque fittings (M) ** Iron fittings (M) ** Various other fittings (7 items, gilt bronze saddle fittings included) (M) * Glass plates ** Three intact plates (M) - Possibly raw materials for glass beads. ** 27 fragments (M19, others: 8+) * Whetstone (M) * Openwork gilt bronze crown (M) * Glass beads (large, medium) - Total: 265 (M256, others: 6). Made of lead glass, semi-transparent green. * Gold rings - Total: 3 (M1, others: 2) * Copper bells - Total: 3 (M2, others: 1) * Copper nails - Total: 4 (M) * Decorative metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Other metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Copper chain - 1 unit (18 links) (M) * Copper vessels - Total: 2 (M). Includes one copper bowl with a lid and one tray. * Copper utility knife with sheath fittings (M) * [[Sue pottery]] - Total: 17 (M4, others: 13). Includes six bowls, five lids, two tall stemmed vessels, and one flat bottle. Older Sue pottery types (before the Oda IVA period, TK209 type) are excluded{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. * [[Haji pottery]] - Total: 3 (M). Includes one bowl and two jars. == Burial Individual ==

({{Supra|40}} {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu}})|02={{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||!}} {{familytree|border=0||||01| 01={{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The individual buried in the Miyajidake Kofun is unknown, but they are presumed to be a chief of the ancient Munakata clan (宗形氏/宗像氏) from the Munakata region. Specifically, one theory identifies the buried individual as '''{{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi}}''' (むなかたのきみとくぜん). Munakata Tokuyoshi is believed to have been the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子}} (654?–696). According to the genealogical records in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, in the second year of Emperor Tenmu (673), Prince Ōama (later {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu}}) married Amako no Iratsume, the daughter of Munakata Tokuyoshi, producing Prince Takechi. While details are sparse due to limited mentions in other texts, Prince Takechi played a central role as the commander-in-chief of Emperor Ōama's forces during the Jinshin War and was later appointed {{ill|Daijō-daijin|ja|太政大臣}} in 690 under Empress Jitō. Munakata Tokuyoshi is therefore thought to have been instrumental in advancing the Munakata clan's influence within the central government「Munakata Tokuyoshi」『Dictionary of Ancient Japanese Clans, Popular Edition』, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2010.. Prince Takechi died in 696, with records in the {{ill|Kuge Bunin|ja|Kugyō補任}} stating he was 42 or 43 years old, while the {{ill|Fusō Ryakki|ja|扶桑略記}} records his age as 43. This suggests he was born around 654, placing Amako no Iratsume's marriage prior to that「Munakata Taisha」『Place names of Fukuoka Prefecture』, Japanese Historical Place names Series 41, Heibonsha, 2004.. No burial goods identifying a specific individual have been excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun. However, considering its relationship with the nearby Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun and Miyajidake Cremation Tomb, a connection to the ancient Munakata clan is plausible{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == Miyajidake Cremation Tomb == The '''Miyajidake Cremation Tomb''' (みやじだけかそうぼ) is an ancient {{ill|Cremation tomb|ja|火葬墓}} believed to have been located near the {{ill|Miyajidake Kofun|ja|宮地嶽古墳}}. The tomb was discovered in [[1938]] (Shōwa 13) on the western slope of a hill (approx. 65 meters above sea level) east of the stone chamber’s entrance during reforestation work. A glass funerary urn was unearthed about one shaku (approx. 30 cm) beneath the surface{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The urn was placed inside a ceramic composite jar and contained a glass short-necked urn with a lid, which was encased in a bronze lidded pedestal jar{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Since the ceramics were from a later period, they are considered secondary burial items, and the original tomb's location and structure remain unknown{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The glass funerary urn is similar in design and manufacturing techniques to one found in the grave of {{ill|Fumi no Nemaro|ja|文祢麻呂}} in {{ill|Uda City|ja|宇陀市}}, Nara Prefecture, which was dated to {{ill|Keiun|ja|慶雲}} 4 (707). This suggests the Miyajidake Cremation Tomb was constructed in the early [[8th century]]{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Hypotheses regarding the buried individual include {{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘}}, the daughter of {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善}}, or Munakata Tōjo, who is mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}} as having been appointed governor of Munakata District in [[Wadō|ja|和銅]] 2 (709){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The excavated funerary urn was designation1 a National Treasure in [[1961]] (Shōwa 36). == Historic site == === National Treasures === * burial goods Excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Kyushu National Museum (formerly in the Tokyo National Museum). It is a {{ill|round mound|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} and one of the Kofuns comprising the {{ill|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|ja|津屋崎古墳群|12=draft}}, designation1 as a National Historic site. The burial items excavated from the mound are classified as a National Treasure. This kofun is known for having the second-largest stone chamber in Japan and for the discovery of numerous luxurious burial items. This article also includes information on the [[Miyajidake Kofun#Miyajidake Cremation Tomb|Miyajidake Cremation Tomb]], whose burial items are also designation1 as National Treasures. == Overview == [[File:Fudo Shrine (No.3 of Okunomiya 8 Shrines) in Miyajidake Shrine.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fudō Shrine (Okunomiya of Miyajidake Shrine)}}{{small|The hall of worship is built in front of the stone chamber opening.}}]] Miyajidake Kofun is a large circular Kofun constructed on the southern slope (approximately 55 meters above sea level) of Mount Miyajidake (elevation 180.7 meters) in northern Fukuoka Prefecture{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Nearby, ancient cremation graves associated with Miyajidake are believed to exist, and the surrounding area once featured small Kofuns. On a hill across the Misogi Pond, the {{ill|Miyaji Idenoue Kofun|ja|宮司井手ノ上古墳|12=draft}} is located{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Currently, the site is worshipped as Fudō Shrine, an Okunomiya (inner shrine) of Miyajidake Shrine. The stone chamber was opened in the mid-Edo period, and burial items were excavated multiple times during the Shōwa era. Measured surveys of the chamber were conducted in 1937 and 1996 (Shōwa 12 and Heisei 8), but no full excavation has been carried out. While the Kofun has been modified over time, it is estimated to have originally been a circular mound approximately 35 meters in diameter{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The burial facility is a {{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone sarcophagus|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}}-type horizontal stone chamber, which opens to the east. The chamber, with a total length of 23 meters, is the second-largest of its kind in Japan. Though no excavations have been conducted inside the chamber, burial items believed to have originally been stored there have been discovered nearby, including a gilded bronze-headed tachi sword nearly 3 meters long, a gilded bronze crown, gilded bronze horse gear, glass plates, bronze ware, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}}. These burial goods are notable for their exceptional quality and quantity, and the horse gear and crown, adorned with arabesque patterns, reflect rich international influences. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the mid-7th century, during the {{ill|final stage of the Kofun period|ja|古墳時代終末期|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}} (or in the early to mid-7th century"Evaluation of the Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster > Miyajidake Kofun," *Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster III*, Fukutsu City Board of Education, 2013. / early 7th century{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, TK217-style period). It is widely regarded as the tomb of a leader from the Munakata clan, an ancient clan in the Munakata region. The specific interred individual is often identified as {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|胸肩君徳善|12=draft}}. The combination of the massive stone chamber and the luxurious burial items makes Miyajidake Kofun one of Japan's representative Kofuns. The burial site was designation1 a National Historic site in 2005 (Heisei 17), and its burial items were designation1 a National Treasure in 1952 (Shōwa 27). Access to the interior of the stone chamber is currently restricted except during the three annual grand festivals. == Archaeological History == * In the first year of the [[Kanpō]] era ([[1741]]), the stone chamber was exposed due to a landslide during heavy rain (as documented in the {{ill|Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel|ja|筑前国続風土記拾遺|12=draft}} compiled during the [[Tenpō]] era ([[1830]]–[[1844]])){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In the 4th year of the [[Enkyō]] era ([[1747]]), the deity Fudō Myōō was enshrined at the back of the stone chamber (as documented in the 'Chikuzen Province Fudoki Sequel'){{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. * In [[1930]] (the 5th year of the [[Shōwa]] era), ancillary facilities were constructed around the tumulus in conjunction with the shrine's relocation{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1934]] (Shōwa 9), equestrian gear and swords were excavated during the construction of the shrine office{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On September 18, [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), the equestrian gear was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), an accurate survey of the stone chamber was conducted (by Kagayama Takeshi){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. * In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a glass ossuary was excavated during afforestation work on the eastern side of the tumulus{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On October 25, [[1939]] (Shōwa 14), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (former Category) under the National Treasure Preservation Act. * In [[1951]] (Shōwa 26), fragments of a crown were excavated in front of the dromos{{Sfn|Miyajidake Kofun (Heibonsha)|2004}}. ** On March 29, [[1952]] (Shōwa 27), the excavated burial goods were designation1 as National Treasures (new Category). ** On April 27, [[1961]] (Shōwa 36), the ossuary was designation1 as a National Treasure (new Category). * In [[1996]] (Heisei 8), the stone chamber was resurveyed (by Ikenoue Hiroshi and others, reported in [[1999]]){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. ** On March 2, [[2005]] (Heisei 17), it was designation1 as a [[Historic site]] of Japan as part of the "[[Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster]]"{{National Heritage Database|401|3422|Tsuyazaki Kofun Cluster}}. == Mound == [[File:Miyajidake-Kofun 20161014.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}{{small|Today, stone rows encircle the mound.}}]] The mound was built by cutting through the gentle slope of a ridge and reshaping the natural terrain{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The current mound has an elliptical type, measuring 27 meters north-south and 34 meters east-west, but it is estimated to have originally been a circular type with a diameter of about 35 meters{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A secondary layer of earth, approximately 2 meters thick, is observed on the mound, which is believed to be the soil excavated during the 1934 digging of the stone chamber{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Around the mound, rows of stones about 1 meter wide and 1.4 meters high encircle the structure, with three-tiered stacking near the dromos{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. These stone rows were installed before 1934 and are believed to have reduced the original size of the mound{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == burial == [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-1.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Bird's-eye view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Miyajidake Kofun, 3D-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Expanded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility is a {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber with a side entrance|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}} type {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening towards the east. Among the passageway and main chamber, the rear section of the main chamber is slightly narrower, divided into a rear chamber and a front chamber, showcasing a multi-chamber structure similar to horizontal stone chambers in the Kinai region. The area of the stone chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}: * Total length of the stone chamber: Approx. 23.1 meters (current measurement: 23.5–24 meters) * Stone sarcophagus (rear chamber): Length 3.5 meters, width approx. 1.75 meters * Main chamber (front chamber): Length 11.7 meters, width 2.5–2.8 meters, height 2.2–3.1 meters ** Left niche (south niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.5 meters ** Right niche (north niche): Length 1.9 meters, depth 0.7 meters, height 1.3 meters The stone material for the chamber is said to be conglomerate rock from the Koi no Ura coast{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Large stones were used, suggesting significant labor was required to transport them from the coast to the mid-slope area{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. The stone chamber is the second largest nationwide after the {{ill|Maruyama Kofun (Kashihara)|ja|丸山古墳 (橿原市)|12=draft}} (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture), with a total length of 28.4 meters. In the stone sarcophagus (first stone from the rear), three approximately 3-meter monolithic stones are assembled. The main chamber (second to fourth stones from the rear) features monolithic stones, 3.1–4.5 meters in height, standing side by side on both sidewalls{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Particularly on the second stone from the rear, niches have been carved into both sides of the stone, which is the largest stone in the chamber, measuring more than 1.7 meters in thickness{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Historical records from the Edo period indicate that these niches existed from the beginning{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The passageway (fifth to seventh stones from the rear) is constructed with two to three layers of stacked stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Near the entrance, stones 0.3–0.4 meters in size are irregularly piled, considered to be secondary stonework{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The floor, currently covered with concrete, was likely originally paved with pebbles and arranged with floor stones{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The ceiling stones measure 0.5 meters thick in the sarcophagus area, 1 meter above the second stone (niche area), and 1.65 meters above the fourth stone{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. A similar stone chamber structure to the Miyajidake Kofun is known from the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳|12=draft}} in Fukutsu City. Previously, the Miyajidake Kofun was thought to precede the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}, but based on investigations from 2010–2011 (Heisei 22–23), it is now hypothesized that the Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun predates the Miyajidake Kofun{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Reference: Bird's-eye view of the {{ill|Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun|ja|手光波切不動古墳|12=draft}} stone chamber Miyajidake Kofun, sekkaku.jpg|Stone sarcophagus and main chamber (towards the rear wall)
{{small|The rear sarcophagus stone is the first stone. Niches are formed on the sidewalls of the second stone in the main chamber.}} Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-1.jpg|Main chamber (towards the rear wall) Miyajidake Kofun, genshitsu-2.jpg|Main chamber (towards the entrance) Miyajidake Kofun, entrance.jpg|Entrance area (towards the rear wall) == burial goods == [[File:HARNESS MIYAJIDAKE.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Gilt Bronze Stirrup (National Treasure)}}]] The grave goods excavated near the tumulus during the Shōwa period are as follows{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Items owned by Miyajidake Shrine (formerly stored in the Tokyo National Museum, later deposited in the Kyushu National Museum, and designation1 as National Treasures) are marked with an "M." * Swords ** Large gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 2.4–2.8 meters. Parts including the pommel, guard, sheath fittings, and blade remain. ** Gilt bronze hilted sword (M) - Estimated length: 0.90 meters. Parts including the pommel, habaki fitting, sheath tip fitting, and blade remain. * Horse gear ** Gilt bronze saddle fittings (M) - Front and rear bridges are mostly intact, but most other fittings are missing. ** Gilt bronze stirrups (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze bridles with decorative plates (pair) (M) ** Gilt bronze pendants (pair) (M) ** Saddle with arabesque fittings (M) ** Iron fittings (M) ** Various other fittings (7 items, gilt bronze saddle fittings included) (M) * Glass plates ** Three intact plates (M) - Possibly raw materials for glass beads. ** 27 fragments (M19, others: 8+) * Whetstone (M) * Openwork gilt bronze crown (M) * Glass beads (large, medium) - Total: 265 (M256, others: 6). Made of lead glass, semi-transparent green. * Gold rings - Total: 3 (M1, others: 2) * Copper bells - Total: 3 (M2, others: 1) * Copper nails - Total: 4 (M) * Decorative metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Other metal fittings - Total: 2 (M) * Copper chain - 1 unit (18 links) (M) * Copper vessels - Total: 2 (M). Includes one copper bowl with a lid and one tray. * Copper utility knife with sheath fittings (M) * [[Sue pottery]] - Total: 17 (M4, others: 13). Includes six bowls, five lids, two tall stemmed vessels, and one flat bottle. Older Sue pottery types (before the Oda IVA period, TK209 type) are excluded{{Sfn|Kojima Atsushi|2018}}. * [[Haji pottery]] - Total: 3 (M). Includes one bowl and two jars. == Burial Individual ==
'''Genealogical chart based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}''' {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||01| 01={{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi|12=draft}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||!|}} {{familytree|border=0|01|~|y|~|02| 01=Ōama no Ōji
({{Supra|40}} {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft}})|02={{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘|12=draft}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||!}} {{familytree|border=0||||01| 01={{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子|12=draft}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The individual buried in the Miyajidake Kofun is unknown, but they are presumed to be a chief of the ancient Munakata clan (宗形氏/宗像氏) from the Munakata region. Specifically, one theory identifies the buried individual as '''{{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|lt=Munakata no Kimi Tokuyoshi|12=draft}}''' (むなかたのきみとくぜん). Munakata Tokuyoshi is believed to have been the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Prince Takechi|ja|高市皇子|12=draft}} (654?–696). According to the genealogical records in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, in the second year of Emperor Tenmu (673), Prince Ōama (later {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft}}) married Amako no Iratsume, the daughter of Munakata Tokuyoshi, producing Prince Takechi. While details are sparse due to limited mentions in other texts, Prince Takechi played a central role as the commander-in-chief of Emperor Ōama's forces during the Jinshin War and was later appointed {{ill|Daijō-daijin|ja|太政大臣|12=draft}} in 690 under Empress Jitō. Munakata Tokuyoshi is therefore thought to have been instrumental in advancing the Munakata clan's influence within the central government「Munakata Tokuyoshi」『Dictionary of Ancient Japanese Clans, Popular Edition』, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2010.. Prince Takechi died in 696, with records in the {{ill|Kuge Bunin|ja|Kugyō補任|12=draft}} stating he was 42 or 43 years old, while the {{ill|Fusō Ryakki|ja|扶桑略記|12=draft}} records his age as 43. This suggests he was born around 654, placing Amako no Iratsume's marriage prior to that「Munakata Taisha」『Place names of Fukuoka Prefecture』, Japanese Historical Place names Series 41, Heibonsha, 2004.. No burial goods identifying a specific individual have been excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun. However, considering its relationship with the nearby Tebika Namikirifudo Kofun and Miyajidake Cremation Tomb, a connection to the ancient Munakata clan is plausible{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. == Miyajidake Cremation Tomb == The '''Miyajidake Cremation Tomb''' (みやじだけかそうぼ) is an ancient {{ill|Cremation tomb|ja|火葬墓|12=draft}} believed to have been located near the {{ill|Miyajidake Kofun|ja|宮地嶽古墳|12=draft}}. The tomb was discovered in [[1938]] (Shōwa 13) on the western slope of a hill (approx. 65 meters above sea level) east of the stone chamber’s entrance during reforestation work. A glass funerary urn was unearthed about one shaku (approx. 30 cm) beneath the surface{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The urn was placed inside a ceramic composite jar and contained a glass short-necked urn with a lid, which was encased in a bronze lidded pedestal jar{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Since the ceramics were from a later period, they are considered secondary burial items, and the original tomb's location and structure remain unknown{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The glass funerary urn is similar in design and manufacturing techniques to one found in the grave of {{ill|Fumi no Nemaro|ja|文祢麻呂|12=draft}} in {{ill|Uda City|ja|宇陀市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, which was dated to {{ill|Keiun|ja|慶雲|12=draft}} 4 (707). This suggests the Miyajidake Cremation Tomb was constructed in the early [[8th century]]{{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. Hypotheses regarding the buried individual include {{ill|Amako no Iratsume|ja|尼子娘|12=draft}}, the daughter of {{ill|Munakata Tokuyoshi|ja|宗形徳善|12=draft}}, or Munakata Tōjo, who is mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}} as having been appointed governor of Munakata District in [[Wadō|ja|和銅]] 2 (709){{Sfn|Ikenoue Hiroshi & Hanada Katsuhiro|1999}}. The excavated funerary urn was designation1 a National Treasure in [[1961]] (Shōwa 36). == Historic site == === National Treasures === * burial goods Excavated from the Miyajidake Kofun (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Kyushu National Museum (formerly in the Tokyo National Museum). Designated as a National Treasure on September 18, [[1936]], under the National Treasure Preservation Act; reclassified as Important Cultural Property under the [[Historic site Protection Law]] in [[1950]]; designation1 as a National Treasure on March 29, [[1952]]{{National Heritage Database|201|841|Miyajidake Kofun burial goods}}. * Glass Ossuary Excavated from the Grounds of Miyajidake Shrine (archaeological materials) **: Details listed below. Owned by Miyajidake Shrine, stored in the Tokyo National Museum.
